be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

derivations.claim: Choose a finite purification $|\Omega\rangle_{ZAF}$ of $\omega_{ZA}$ by [F1] and reorder its factors as $A(ZF)$. Let $\rho_A=\sum_{j=1}^r\lambda_j|a_j\rangle\langle a_j|$ be a spectral decomposition on its positive support, obtained from [F7]. Expand each purification in the product basis using this same eigenbasis on $A$: $$|\psi\rangle_{RA}=\sum_{j=1}^r|r_j^0\rangle_R|a_j\rangle_A,\qquad |\Omega\rangle_{A(ZF)}=\sum_{j=1}^r|a_j\rangle_A|z_j^0\rangle_{ZF}.$$ The partial-trace coordinate formula [F2] and the fact that both $A$ marginals equal $\rho_A$ show that the coefficient vectors have Gram matrices $\langle r_j^0,r_k^0\rangle=\lambda_j\delta_{jk}$ and $\langle z_j^0,z_k^0\rangle=\lambda_j\delta_{jk}$. Thus $|r_j\rangle:=|r_j^0\rangle/\sqrt{\lambda_j}$ and $|z_j\rangle:=|z_j^0\rangle/\sqrt{\lambda_j}$ are orthonormal and $$|\psi\rangle_{RA}=\sum_{j=1}^r\sqrt{\lambda_j}|r_j\rangle_R|a_j\rangle_A,\qquad |\Omega\rangle_{A(ZF)}=\sum_{j=1}^r\sqrt{\lambda_j}|a_j\rangle_A|z_j\rangle_{ZF}.$$ This coefficient argument also handles repeated positive eigenvalues because the chosen basis is fixed before either expansion.

Let $d=\dim R=\dim A$. In every case set $G=\mathbb C^d$, fix its first coordinate unit vector $|0\rangle_G$, and append it to $|\Omega\rangle$. Since $Z$ and the purifying space $F$ are nonzero, $\dim(Z\otimes F\otimes G)\ge d$. Denote the resulting orthonormal Schmidt partners by $|z_j'\rangle=|z_j\rangle|0\rangle_G$. The map $U_0:\operatorname{span}\{|r_j\rangle}\to\operatorname{span}\{|z_j'\rangle\}$ given by $U_0|r_j\rangle=|z_j'\rangle$ is an isometry. Extend $\{|r_j\rangle\}$ to an orthonormal basis of $R$ and choose the same number of additional orthonormal vectors in the orthogonal complement of the $z_j'$ in $Z\otimes F\otimes G$; [F5] and the target dimension bound ensure this is possible. Sending the added basis vectors to those target vectors extends $U_0$ to a linear isometry $U:R\to Z\otimes F\otimes G$ on all of $R$. By construction, $(U\otimes I_A)|\psi\rangle$ is exactly the padded purification $|\Omega\rangle\otimes|0\rangle_G$, after reordering to $Z(F\otimes G)A$. This construction includes the singular case $r<d$, since it extends $U$ on all zero-Schmidt directions of $R$.

Define $\Lambda(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_{F\otimes G}(UXU^*)$ from $\mathcal L(R)$ to $\mathcal L(Z)$. Since $U$ is an isometry, [F4] makes $\Lambda$ completely positive and trace-preserving on the full operator space. Applying it to the reference factor of $|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$ traces $F\otimes G$ from the pure state $|(U\otimes I_A)\psi\rangle\langle(U\otimes I_A)\psi|$, leaving its $ZA$ marginal, which is $\omega_{ZA}$ by construction and is unchanged by the appended pure $G$ register [F6]. Thus $(\Lambda\otimes\operatorname{id}_A)(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)=\omega_{ZA}$, as required.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F1] [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]: Finite-dimensional von Neumann entropy.
citations.quote:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F2] [[thm-it-quantum-relative-entropy-nonnegative-equality]]: Nonnegativity and equality for finite quantum relative entropy.
citations.quote:
For density operators $\rho,\sigma$ on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space,

$$D(\rho\|\sigma)\ge0,$$

with equality if and only if $\rho=\sigma$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F3] [[thm-qc-schmidt-decomposition]]: Schmidt decomposition.
citations.quote:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex-inner-product spaces with the tensor-product convention of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For every $\Psi\in H\otimes K$ there are an integer $r\ge0$, positive numbers $s_1,\ldots,s_r$, and orthonormal families $u_1,\ldots,u_r\in H$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_r\in K$ such that

$$\Psi=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j u_j\otimes v_j,\qquad \|\Psi\|^2=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j^2.$$

For $\Psi=0$ take $r=0$ and the empty sum. For any chosen ordered pair of orthonormal bases, the construction below obtains the $s_j$ as the positive singular values of the coefficient matrix of $\Psi$ in their ordered product basis.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F4] [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]: 'The basis-independent trace of an endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space'.
citations.quote:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F5] [[thm-non-negative-operator-characterisations]]: if $T$ is non-negative and $\langle Tv,v\rangle=0$, then $Tv=0$.
citations.quote:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space and let
$T:V\to V$ be linear. The following are equivalent:

1. $T$ is non-negative.
2. $T$ is self-adjoint and every eigenvalue of $T$ is a nonnegative real number.
3. Some orthonormal basis makes the matrix of $T$ diagonal with nonnegative real diagonal entries.
4. There exists a linear map $S:V\to V$ such that $T=S^*S$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F6] [[def-it-finite-dimensional-quantum-relative-entropy]] and [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]: on support inclusion, $D(\alpha\|\beta)=\operatorname{tr}(\alpha\ln\alpha)-\operatorname{tr}(\alpha\ln\beta)$, and $\ln(xy)=\ln x+\ln y$ for positive $x,y$.
citations.quote:
Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $A,B:H\to H$ be non-negative operators. For such an operator $A$, set $\operatorname{supp}(A):=(\ker A)^\perp$, where $\ker A$ is the kernel of a linear map ([[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]); this extends the density-operator support convention in [[def-qc-density-operator]]. If $\operatorname{supp}(A)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(B)$, define

$$D(A\|B):=\operatorname{tr}(A\ln A)-\operatorname{tr}(A\ln B).$$

Here $\ln A$ is defined spectrally on the positive eigenspaces of $A$ with $0\ln0:=0$, and $\ln B$ in the cross term is restricted to $\operatorname{supp}(B)$; the support condition ensures that $A$ vanishes on $\ker B$, so the omitted kernel contributes zero. If $\operatorname{supp}(A)\nsubseteq\operatorname{supp}(B)$, set $D(A\|B):=+\infty$. In particular, $D(0\|B)=0$. For density operators this is the finite-dimensional **quantum relative entropy**. The logarithms are natural, so the value is in nats; the base-two value is $D_2(A\|B):=D(A\|B)/\ln2$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F6] [[def-it-finite-dimensional-quantum-relative-entropy]] and [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]: on support inclusion, $D(\alpha\|\beta)=\operatorname{tr}(\alpha\ln\alpha)-\operatorname{tr}(\alpha\ln\beta)$, and $\ln(xy)=\ln x+\ln y$ for positive $x,y$.
citations.quote:
The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,
$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

derivations.claim: Omit zero weights. For each $i$ with $p_i>0$, $\bar\rho-p_i\rho_i=\sum_{j\ne i}p_j\rho_j$ is non-negative. If $v\in\ker\bar\rho$, its quadratic form under this sum is zero; every summand is nonnegative, so $\langle\rho_i v,v\rangle=0$ and [F5] gives $\rho_i v=0$. Hence $\operatorname{supp}\rho_i\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\bar\rho$ and every $D(\rho_i\|\bar\rho)$ is finite. The trace formula [F6], linearity of trace [F4], and $\bar\rho=\sum_i p_i\rho_i$ give $$\sum_i p_iD(\rho_i\Vert\bar\rho)=S(\bar\rho)-\sum_i p_iS(\rho_i)\ge0$$ by [F2].

For the upper bound, diagonalize each $\rho_i=\sum_j\lambda_{ij}|v_{ij}\rangle\langle v_{ij}|$, omitting zero weights and eigenvalues, and purify the mixture as $|v\rangle=\sum_{ij}\sqrt{p_i\lambda_{ij}}|v_{ij}\rangle\otimes|i,j\rangle$. Its label marginal $G$ is a state with diagonal $q_{ij}=p_i\lambda_{ij}$ and has the same nonzero eigenvalues as $\bar\rho$ by Schmidt decomposition. The logarithm product law in [F6] gives $H(q)=H(p)+\sum_i p_iS(\rho_i)$.

For $\Delta=\operatorname{diag}(q)$, its kernel is spanned by coordinate labels with $q_{ij}=0$. Each such basis vector $e_{ij}$ has $\langle Ge_{ij},e_{ij}\rangle=q_{ij}=0$, so [F5] gives $Ge_{ij}=0$. Hence $G$ annihilates $\ker\Delta$ and $\operatorname{supp}G\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\Delta$. The formula [F6] now gives $$0\le D(G\Vert\Delta)=H(q)-S(G)=H(p)+\sum_i p_iS(\rho_i)-S(\bar\rho).$$ This proves both bounds, including singleton/zero-weight cases.

Let $(a_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a real sequence with $a_0=0$, $a_{m+n}\ge a_m+a_n$ for all $m,n\ge0$, and $|a_n|\le Cn$ for some finite constant $C$. Then

$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{a_n}{n}=\sup_{k\ge1}\frac{a_k}{k}.$$

derivations.claim: Set $\alpha:=\sup_{k\ge1}a_k/k$. The bound in [A1] makes $\alpha$ finite, and the definition of supremum gives $a_n/n\le\alpha$ for every $n\ge1$. Hence $\limsup_{n\to\infty}a_n/n\le\alpha$.

Fix $k\ge1$. For each $n$, write $n=qk+r$ with integers $q\ge0$ and $0\le r<k$. Repeated use of superadditivity in [A1] gives $a_n\ge qa_k+a_r$. The finitely many values $a_0,\ldots,a_{k-1}$ have a finite minimum $m_k$, so $a_n/n\ge(q/n)a_k+m_k/n$. As $n\to\infty$, $q/n\to1/k$ and $m_k/n\to0$, yielding $\liminf_{n\to\infty}a_n/n\ge a_k/k$.
Since step 1.2 holds for every $k\ge1$, taking the supremum gives $\liminf_{n\to\infty}a_n/n\ge\alpha$. Combining with step 1.1 proves the asserted limit and its value.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F2] [[thm-qc-trace-norm-duality-and-norm-properties]]: Trace Norm Duality And Norm Properties.

Let $A:H\to K$ be a linear map ([[def-linear-map]]) between finite-dimensional complex
inner-product spaces. If $U:K\to K$ and $V:H\to H$ are unitary, then
$\|UAV\|_1=\|A\|_1$. If $P:H\to H$ is non-negative (positive semidefinite),
then

$$\|P\|_1=\operatorname{tr}_H(P).$$

Here non-negative means self-adjoint with
$\langle Pv,v\rangle\ge0$ for all $v$, as in
[[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]].

citations.exact_fact_text: [F8] [[thm-qc-hermitian-trace-norm-positive-negative-parts]]: a Hermitian operator is the difference of positive and negative parts and its trace norm is the sum of their traces.
citations.quote:
Let $\mathcal H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let
$X:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H$ be self-adjoint. There are non-negative
endomorphisms $X_+,X_-$ such that

$$X=X_+-X_-,\qquad \langle X_+u,X_-v\rangle=0\quad(u,v\in\mathcal H),$$

and

$$\|X\|_1=\operatorname{tr}(X_+)+\operatorname{tr}(X_-).$$

If $\operatorname{tr}(X)=0$, then
$\|X\|_1=2\operatorname{tr}(X_+)=2\operatorname{tr}(X_-)$. 

The trace norm is the finite singular-value norm from
[[def-qc-trace-norm]].

derivations.claim: Set $\zeta=\exp(2\pi i/5)$. The three finite complex-exponential premises in [F9] show $|\zeta|=1$ and $\zeta^m=1$ exactly when $5$ divides $m$. Let $G$ be the finite group of monomial unitaries whose nonzero entries belong to $\{1,\zeta,\zeta^2,\zeta^3,\zeta^4\}$. Let $R$ be the real rotation by $\pi/4$ in coordinates 1 and 2, acting identically elsewhere. Use the symmetric finite list $\mathcal S=G\cup\{R,R^*\}$, retaining multiplicities if any. At each walk step choose the identity with probability $1/2$ and an element of this list uniformly with the remaining probability. For $j=1,2$, the moment operator on matrices is $$T_j(X)=\tfrac12X+\frac1{2|\mathcal S|}\sum_{U\in\mathcal S}U^{\otimes j}X(U^*)^{\otimes j}.$$ These are self-adjoint contractions for the Hilbert–Schmidt inner product, because the list is inverse-symmetric; laziness makes every eigenvalue nonnegative. Moreover $$\langle X,(I-T_j)X\rangle=\frac1{4|\mathcal S|}\sum_{U\in\mathcal S}\|X-U^{\otimes j}X(U^*)^{\otimes j}\|_2^2.$$ Thus their fixed spaces are exactly the simultaneous commutants of the displayed finite unitaries.

For $j=1$, the independent diagonal fifth-root phases force a commuting matrix to be diagonal; permutations force all its diagonal entries equal. For $j=2$, a matrix coefficient from $|i,j\rangle$ to $|k,l\rangle$ can survive the diagonal phases only when the unordered multisets $\{i,j\}$ and $\{k,l\}$ agree. By the primitive-order identity established in step 1.1, each index occurs with multiplicity 0, 1 or 2; equality modulo 5 of every exponent forces equality of these integer multiplicities. Commutation with all permutations then leaves three constants: $c$ on $|i,i\rangle$, $a$ on $|i,j\rangle\langle i,j|$ for $i\ne j$, and $b$ on $|i,j\rangle\langle j,i|$. Commutation with $R\otimes R$ applied to $|1,1\rangle$, whose rotated vector has nonzero coefficients on both $|1,2\rangle$ and $|2,1\rangle$, forces $c=a+b$. Conversely $I$ and the swap $F$ commute with every tensor-square unitary. The fixed space is therefore precisely $\operatorname{span}\{I,F\}$, also when $D=2$.

Finite-dimensional spectral decomposition now gives orthogonal projections $\mathcal P_1,\mathcal P_2$ onto these fixed spaces and a number $0\le\lambda<1$ such that $$\|T_j^L-\mathcal P_j\|_{2\to2}\le\lambda^L,\qquad j=1,2.$$ If the orthogonal complement is zero, take its spectral radius as zero. Every $T_j^L$ is the moment of an finite distribution of length-$L$ unitary words; the limit is only a finite-matrix spectral calculation, not an assumed Haar integral. The first projection is $\mathcal P_1(X)=\operatorname{tr}(X)I/D$. For any rank-$K$ projection $P_0$, invariance of trace and swap trace gives $$\mathcal P_2(P_0\otimes P_0)=a_0I+b_0F,\qquad a_0=\frac{K(KD-1)}{D(D^2-1)},\quad b_0=\frac{K(D-K)}{D(D^2-1)}.$$ The coefficients solve $a_0D^2+b_0D=K^2$ and $a_0D+b_0D^2=K$.

Choose a coordinate isometry $W_0$ and let $W=UW_0$, where $U$ is a finite walk word. Complex conjugation preserves the same limiting first and second moment projections and their norm bounds, so they apply to $P=\overline W W^T$ as well. The swap identity on matrix units gives the following limiting second moment, with $\Omega=I_R/K\otimes\omega_E$: $$\lim_{L\to\infty}\mathbb E\|\omega^W-\Omega\|_2^2 =\frac{D(KD-1)}{K(D^2-1)}\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)+\frac{1-DK}{K(D^2-1)}\operatorname{tr}(\omega_E^2) \le2\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2).$$ In detail, the squared-state term is $(D^2/K^2)\{a_0\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)+b_0\operatorname{tr}(\omega_E^2)\}$, and the limiting mean is $\Omega$, so subtract $\operatorname{tr}(\omega_E^2)/K$.

The finite moment error has a quantitative bound. Put $d_E=\dim E$ and $\varepsilon=\lambda^L$. The first-moment error in each matrix unit of the compressed reference is at most $\varepsilon$ in Hilbert–Schmidt norm; contracting it with $\omega$ shows $\|\mathbb E\omega^W-\Omega\|_2\le D\varepsilon\|\omega\|_2\le D\varepsilon$. For the squared-state term, the second-moment error on $P_0\otimes P_0$ has Hilbert–Schmidt norm at most $K\varepsilon$. In its trace pairing with $F_E(\omega\otimes\omega)$, the partial trace over the two environment copies has Hilbert–Schmidt norm at most $d_E\|\omega\|_2^2\le d_E$ (Cauchy–Schwarz for each diagonal block). Consequently that squared-state error is at most $D^2d_E\varepsilon/K$. The cross term with $\Omega$, whose Hilbert–Schmidt norm is at most $1/\sqrt K$, has error at most $2D\varepsilon/\sqrt K$. Hence, with $C_D=D^2d_E+2D$, $$\mathbb E\|\omega^W-\Omega\|_2^2\le2\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)+C_D\varepsilon.$$ Positivity implies $\operatorname{supp}\omega\subseteq A\otimes\operatorname{supp}\omega_E$: if $v\in\ker\omega_E$, the marginal quadratic form is a sum of nonnegative diagonal quadratic forms of $\omega$; each is zero, and [F6] makes the corresponding product vectors kernel vectors of $\omega$. Self-adjointness then makes the corresponding rows and columns zero. Compression acts only on $A$, so both $\omega^W$ and $\Omega$ are supported in $\mathbb C^K\otimes\operatorname{supp}\omega_E$; each difference therefore has rank at most $Kr$. Cauchy–Schwarz on singular values and Jensen give the trace-norm bound at most $\sqrt{2Kr\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)}+\sqrt{KrC_D\varepsilon}$.

Finally write a Hermitian $Z$ as $Z_+-Z_-$ using [F8]. Each compression of $Z_+$ or $Z_-$ is positive, so its trace norm is its trace by [F7]; positivity and linearity therefore bound the trace norm of the difference by the sum of the two compressed traces. The first-moment bound $\|\mathbb EP-(K/D)I\|_\infty\le\sqrt K\varepsilon$ gives $$\mathbb E\|\mathcal C_W(Z)\|_1\le(1+D\varepsilon/\sqrt K)\|Z\|_1.$$ Choose a finite $L$ with both $KrC_D\lambda^L\le\delta^2$ and $D\lambda^L/\sqrt K\le\delta$. Such an integer exists by $\lambda<1$; the least such integer is a specified choice. If $r=0$, the positive operator is zero and its decoupling bound is automatic. This proves both assertions with an finite ensemble and exact dimension-dependent moment control.

source_export.quote:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $\tau$ be a density operator on $H$, let $e$ be a unit vector orthogonal to the data summand in $H\oplus\mathbb C e$, and let $p\in[0,1]$. With $h(p):=-p\ln p-(1-p)\ln(1-p)$ and $0\ln0:=0$, the block-diagonal state

$$\omega_p:=p\tau\oplus(1-p)|e\rangle\langle e|$$

satisfies $S(\omega_p)=h(p)+pS(\tau)$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F1] [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]: entropy is $-\sum_{\lambda>0}\lambda\ln\lambda$, and zero-eigenvalue terms contribute zero.
citations.quote:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F2] [[def-qc-density-operator]] and [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]: $\tau$ has nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ summing to one, with an orthonormal eigenbasis.
citations.quote:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$; non-negative and trace have the meanings of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]] and [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F2] [[def-qc-density-operator]] and [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]: $\tau$ has nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ summing to one, with an orthonormal eigenbasis.
citations.quote:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F3] [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]: $\ln(xy)=\ln x+\ln y$ for positive $x,y$, and $\ln1=0$.
citations.quote:
The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,
$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

derivations.claim: The orthogonal summands reduce $\omega_p$, so its eigenvalues, including multiplicities, are $p\lambda_j$ on $H$ and $1-p$ on the flag. For $0<p<1$, [F1]–[F3] give $S(\omega_p)=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}p\lambda_j\ln(p\lambda_j)-(1-p)\ln(1-p)=h(p)+pS(\tau)$, because $\sum_j\lambda_j=1$.

At $p=0$, $\omega_p$ is the pure flag state and both sides equal zero. At $p=1$, $\omega_p=\tau$ and both sides equal $S(\tau)$. Thus the formula holds on the closed interval, including its endpoints.

source_export.quote: Let $\mathcal N:\mathcal L(A)\to\mathcal L(B)$ be a finite-dimensional channel with $d=\dim A\ge1$. Fix a Stinespring isometry $V:A\to B\otimes E$ satisfying $\mathcal N(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^*)$ for every $X$, and set $\mathcal N^c(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)$ and $\tau=I_A/d$. Every $0<R<I_c(\tau,\mathcal N)$ is achievable by isometric subspace entanglement transmission; if $I_c(\tau,\mathcal N)\le0$, rate zero is achieved by a one-dimensional code. An $n$-use code has an isometry $W_n:\mathbb C^{K_n}\to A^{\otimes n}$ and a CPTP decoder to $\mathbb C^{K_n}$; its squared overlap with the maximally entangled target tends to one and $n^{-1}\ln K_n\to R$. More generally, for any isometric inclusion $J:\mathbb C^D\to A$ with $D\ge1$, the same conclusion holds for the flat state $JJ^*/D$ by applying the result to $X\mapsto\mathcal N(JXJ^*)$ and composing encoders with $J^{\otimes n}$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F1] [[lem-it-finite-unitary-averaging-decoupling-bound]]: Finite unitary averaging and a decoupling second-moment bound.
citations.quote:
Let $D\ge2$, $1\le K\le D$, and $\omega_{AE}\succeq0$ with $\dim A=D$, $\operatorname{tr}\omega\le1$, and $r=\operatorname{rank}\omega_E$. For every $\delta>0$ there is an explicitly specified finite probability ensemble of isometries $W:\mathbb C^K\to\mathbb C^D$ such that, for
$$\omega^W_{RE}=\frac DK(W^T\otimes I_E)\omega_{AE}(\overline W\otimes I_E),$$
one has
$$\mathbb E\left\|\omega^W_{RE}-\frac{I_R}{K}\otimes\omega_E\right\|_1\le\sqrt{2Kr\operatorname{tr}(\omega_{AE}^2)}+\delta.$$
At the same time the ensemble can be required to satisfy, for every Hermitian $Z_{AE}$,
$$\mathbb E\left\|\frac DK(W^T\otimes I)Z(\overline W\otimes I)\right\|_1\le(1+\delta)\|Z\|_1.$$
No Haar existence or Gaussian-law supplier, and no choice axiom, is used.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F2] [[lem-it-exponential-cq-spectral-projectors]]: Exponential averaged spectral projectors for a finite cq ensemble.
citations.quote:
For every fixed finite ensemble $p_x,\rho_x$ and fixed $\eta>0$, there are constants $C,c>0$ (depending on this ensemble and $\eta$, not $n$) and projectors $P_n,Q_{x^n}$ such that, writing $\bar\rho=\sum p_x\rho_x$ and $s=\sum p_xS(\rho_x)$,
$$\operatorname{rank}P_n\le e^{n(S(\bar\rho)+\eta)},\quad P_n\bar\rho^{\otimes n}P_n\preceq e^{-n(S(\bar\rho)-\eta)}P_n,$$
$$\operatorname{rank}Q_{x^n}\le e^{n(s+\eta)},\quad Q_{x^n}\rho_{x^n}Q_{x^n}\preceq e^{-n(s-\eta)}Q_{x^n},$$
and
$$\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{X^n}(I-P_n))\le Ce^{-cn},\qquad\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{X^n}(I-Q_{X^n}))\le Ce^{-cn}.$$
The second pair of algebraic bounds holds for every word, including words with zero sampling probability; no per-word high-acceptance assertion is required.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F3] [[lem-it-finite-gentle-measurement]]: Gentle measurement bound in finite dimensions.
citations.quote:
Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$, let $0\preceq\Lambda\preceq I_H$, and suppose $\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda\rho)\ge1-u$ for some $u\in[0,1]$. Then

$$\left\|\rho-\sqrt{\Lambda}\rho\sqrt{\Lambda}\right\|_1\le2\sqrt{u}.$$

Here $\sqrt{\Lambda}$ is the unique nonnegative square root, and $\|\cdot\|_1$ is the finite-dimensional trace norm. No normalization is applied after the operation $\rho\mapsto\sqrt{\Lambda}\rho\sqrt{\Lambda}$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F4] [[thm-qc-finite-stinespring-dilation]]: Every finite-dimensional channel has a finite isometric dilation.
citations.quote:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be a quantum channel. It has a finite
Kraus representation, and for any chosen such representation with $N$
operators $K_a:H\to K$ there are an $N$-dimensional environment $E$ and a
linear isometry $V:H\to K\otimes E$ such that
$$\Phi(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^\dagger)\quad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H).$$

citations.exact_fact_text: [F5] [[thm-qc-schmidt-decomposition]]: Schmidt decomposition.
citations.quote:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex-inner-product spaces with the tensor-product convention of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For every $\Psi\in H\otimes K$ there are an integer $r\ge0$, positive numbers $s_1,\ldots,s_r$, and orthonormal families $u_1,\ldots,u_r\in H$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_r\in K$ such that

$$\Psi=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j u_j\otimes v_j,\qquad \|\Psi\|^2=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j^2.$$

For $\Psi=0$ take $r=0$ and the empty sum. For any chosen ordered pair of orthonormal bases, the construction below obtains the $s_j$ as the positive singular values of the coefficient matrix of $\Psi$ in their ordered product basis.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F6] [[thm-qc-fidelity-purification-characterization]]: Fidelity Purification Characterization.
citations.quote:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\rho,\sigma\in\mathcal D(H)$. For every auxiliary space $R$ with $\dim R\ge\dim H$, a **purification** of $\rho$ on $H\otimes R$ means a unit vector $x$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_R(|x\rangle\langle x|)=\rho$. Then
$$F(\rho,\sigma)=\max\{|\langle x,y\rangle|:x,y\in H\otimes R,\ \|x\|=\|y\|=1,\ \operatorname{Tr}_R|x\rangle\langle x|=\rho,\ \operatorname{Tr}_R|y\rangle\langle y|=\sigma\}.$$
In particular, the maximum is attained with $R\cong H$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F7] [[thm-qc-purification-existence-and-unitary-equivalence]]: Purifications exist and are unitarily equivalent after padding.
citations.quote:
Every density operator $\rho$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space $H$ has a purification on some finite-dimensional auxiliary space. More precisely, if $r=\operatorname{rank}(\rho)$, it has one on an auxiliary space of dimension $r$. If $\Psi_i\in H\otimes K_i$ ($i=1,2$) are any two purifications of the same $\rho$, then for every integer $m\ge\max(\dim K_1,\dim K_2)$ and every pair of linear isometric embeddings $\iota_i:K_i\to\mathbb C^m$, where $\mathbb C^m$ has its standard complex inner product, there is a unitary $U$ on $\mathbb C^m$ such that

$$ (I_H\otimes U)(I_H\otimes\iota_2)\Psi_2=(I_H\otimes\iota_1)\Psi_1. $$

citations.exact_fact_text: [F8] [[thm-qc-fuchs-van-de-graaf]]: Fuchs Van De Graaf.
citations.quote:
For density operators $\rho,\sigma$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space,
$$1-F(\rho,\sigma)\le D(\rho,\sigma)\le\sqrt{1-F(\rho,\sigma)^2},$$
where $F$ is root fidelity and $D(\rho,\sigma)=\tfrac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F9] [[lem-qa-21-partial-trace-contracts-trace-norm-on-hermitians]]: Partial trace contracts the trace norm on Hermitian operators.
citations.quote:
Let $H_A,H_E$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $X=X^\dagger$ be an endomorphism of $H_A\otimes H_E$. Then
$$\|\operatorname{Tr}_E X\|_1\le\|X\|_1.$$
The trace norm and partial trace are those of [[def-qc-trace-norm]] and [[def-qc-partial-trace]]. If either factor is zero-dimensional, both sides are zero.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F10] [[thm-it-finite-strong-subadditivity]]: Strong subadditivity of finite-dimensional quantum entropy.
citations.quote:
Let $H_A,H_B,H_C$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\rho_{ABC}$ be a density operator on their ordered tensor product. Write $\rho_{AB},\rho_{BC},\rho_B$ for its marginals using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]]. Then
$$S(\rho_{AB})+S(\rho_{BC})\ge S(\rho_B)+S(\rho_{ABC}),$$
where $S(\rho)=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho)$ with $0\ln0:=0$ as in [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

citations.exact_fact_text: [F11] [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]] and [[lem-it-quantum-coherent-information-complement-identity]]: for the fixed dilation, $I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\mathcal N^c(\rho))$.
citations.quote:
Let $A$ and $B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\mathcal N:\mathcal L(A)\to\mathcal L(B)$ be a quantum channel as in [[def-qc-quantum-channel]]. Choose a finite-dimensional environment $E$ and a linear isometry $V:A\to B\otimes E$ such that

$$\mathcal N(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^*)$$

for every $X\in\mathcal L(A)$; such a dilation exists by [[thm-qc-finite-stinespring-dilation]]. The channel

$$\mathcal N^c(X):=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)\in\mathcal L(E)$$

is the **complementary channel associated with this chosen dilation**. The partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_B$ contracts the first factor of the ordered product $B\otimes E$ ([[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]).

It is a quantum channel: reorder $B\otimes E$ to $E\otimes B$ by the finite wire-permutation unitary ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]); the reordered $V$ is still an isometry, so tracing its second factor $B$ gives a channel by [[thm-qc-isometry-partial-trace-is-channel]].

For a density operator $\rho$ on $A$, choose a finite purification $|\psi\rangle\in A\otimes R$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_R|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|=\rho$ ([[def-qc-ensemble-and-purification]]), and define $\omega_{BR}:=(\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)$. Its **coherent information** from $A$ to $B$ is

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N):=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\omega_{BR}),$$

where $S$ is finite-dimensional von Neumann entropy in nats ([[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]). The value does not depend on the chosen purification: after padding reference spaces, any two purifications differ by a unitary on $R$ ([[thm-qc-purification-existence-and-unitary-equivalence]]); applying $\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R$ preserves that unitary relation. A unitary maps an orthonormal eigenbasis to an orthonormal eigenbasis with the same eigenvalues, so entropy is unchanged ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]). Padding adds only zero eigenvalues, which do not contribute.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F11] [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]] and [[lem-it-quantum-coherent-information-complement-identity]]: for the fixed dilation, $I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\mathcal N^c(\rho))$.
citations.quote:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional channel, let $V:A\to B\otimes E$ be a finite Stinespring isometry, let $\mathcal N^c(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)$, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $A$. Then

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\mathcal N^c(\rho)).$$

The right-hand side is independent of the chosen Stinespring dilation, since it equals the purification-defined quantity in [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]].

citations.exact_fact_text: [F12] [[lem-it-quantum-entropy-maximized-at-maximally-mixed-state]] and [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]: $S(I_A/d)=\ln d$ and $\exp(\ln d)=d$.
citations.quote:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space of dimension $d$, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$. Then

$$S(\rho)\le\ln d,$$

derivations.claim: Put $s_B=S(\mathcal N(\tau))$ and $s_E=S(\mathcal N^c(\tau))$. By [F11], $s_B-s_E=I_c(\tau,\mathcal N)$; choose $\eta>0$ with $R<s_B-s_E-2\eta$. On $n$ uses, let $|v_n\rangle=(I\otimes V^{\otimes n})|\Phi_{d^n}\rangle$ in factor order $A'B^nE^n$. Let $P_n,Q_n$ be the spectral projectors for the IID receiver and environment states from [[lem-it-exponential-cq-spectral-projectors]], and let $\epsilon_n\le Ce^{-cn}$ bound the sum of their failure probabilities. The commuting joint projection has acceptance at least $1-\epsilon_n$. For $$|\widehat v_n\rangle=(I_{A'}\otimes P_n\otimes Q_n)|v_n\rangle,$$ the rank-two pure-vector calculation used in gentle measurement gives $$\bigl\||v_n\rangle\langle v_n|-|\widehat v_n\rangle\langle\widehat v_n|\bigr\|_1\le2\sqrt{\epsilon_n}.$$ This follows also by applying the gentle-measurement lemma to the pure state and the joint projection. Let $\omega=\operatorname{Tr}_{B^n}|\widehat v_n\rangle\langle\widehat v_n|$. Its environment rank is at most $e^{n(s_E+\eta)}$. Since the projected vector is pure, $$\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)=\operatorname{tr}(\omega_{B^n}^2).$$ Moreover $$0\preceq\omega_{B^n}\preceq P_n\mathcal N(\tau)^{\otimes n}P_n\preceq e^{-n(s_B-\eta)}P_n.$$ To verify the first inequality, take the partial trace after $Q_n$; the complementary environment projection produces another positive summand of the original receiver marginal. Hence $\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)\le e^{-n(s_B-\eta)}$, because its trace is at most one.

First prove $s_B\le\ln d+s_E$. The one-use Stinespring output of $|\Phi_d\rangle$ is pure on $A'BE$, so [F5] gives $s_B=S(A'E)$. For its marginal state $\omega_{A'E}$, append a one-dimensional register $C$ in a pure state and order the resulting state as $A'CE$. Strong subadditivity [F10] gives $S(A'C)+S(CE)\ge S(C)+S(A'CE)$, that is $S(A')+S(E)\ge S(A'E)$; [F12] gives $S(A')=\ln d$. Hence $s_B\le\ln d+s_E$, so $I_c=s_B-s_E\le\ln d$ and $0<R<I_c$ implies $K_n=\lfloor e^{nR}\rfloor\le d^n$ by [F12]. For an isometry $W:\mathbb C^{K_n}\to A^{\otimes n}$, let $\rho^W_{RE^n}$ be the environment/reference state produced by encoding half of $|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle$. Coefficient matrices give exactly the normalized-compression expression for the unprojected marginal. Use the finite ensemble above with tolerance $e^{-n}$. Apply its compression estimate to $\omega$, and its averaged trace-contraction estimate to the difference between projected and unprojected marginals. Their environment marginals differ by at most $2\sqrt{\epsilon_n}$. The triangle inequality therefore yields $$\mathbb E\left\|\rho^W_{RE^n}-\frac{I_R}{K_n}\otimes\mathcal N^c(\tau)^{\otimes n}\right\|_1 \le6\sqrt{\epsilon_n}+2e^{-n}+\sqrt{2e^{-n(s_B-s_E-R-2\eta)}}\longrightarrow0.$$ Order the finite generator list and its length-$L$ words. For each $n$, take the first word whose displayed norm is at most twice its expectation; if that expectation is zero, take the first zero-norm word. A qualifying word exists by finite averaging. This specifies the entire encoder sequence without countable choices.

The product target is purified by $|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle_{RM}\otimes|e_n\rangle_{E^nF}$, with a sufficiently large finite $F$. The encoded Stinespring output is another purification on reference/environment versus receiver. Root-fidelity purification characterization, after adding a pure finite ancilla to the receiver if needed, supplies an isometry on the receiver's purifying space whose overlap with that target is the root fidelity of the two marginals. The fixed-purification form follows from the purification/unitary-equivalence theorem. Fuchs–van de Graaf makes this root fidelity at least one minus half the displayed norm. Trace out the extra decoder factor $F$: the resulting CPTP decoder has squared entanglement fidelity at least the square of that overlap and hence tending to one. The encoder is exactly the isometry $W$; no generating-code/transmitting-code equivalence is assumed. Fix ordered bases throughout. In the purification characterization use the polar/SVD attaining map, extending every kernel partial isometry by the ordered basis completion; in repeated eigenspaces, project the ordered coordinate vectors and Gram–Schmidt in that order. This specifies a decoder at each block length by one formula, rather than choosing a sequence of unrelated attaining maps.

If $I_c(\tau,\mathcal N)\le0$, choose a unit vector of $A^{\otimes n}$ as the encoder for $K_n=1$. The decoder to $\mathbb C$ is $X\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(X)$, a channel by [F13] using the isometry $x\mapsto1\otimes x$ and tracing $A^{\otimes n}$. Its entanglement fidelity is one and its rate is zero. For a subspace inclusion $J:\mathbb C^D\to A$, the restricted channel $\mathcal N_J(X)=\mathcal N(JXJ^*)$ has dilation $VJ$, and its flat input $I_D/D$ has coherent information $I_c(JJ^*/D,\mathcal N)$ by the fixed-dilation definition. source_export.quote: Let $\tau=JJ^*/D$ be the flat state of a nonzero $D$-dimensional input subspace of a finite-dimensional channel $\mathcal N$. With prior shared maximally entangled states on that subspace, every $0\le R<S(\tau)+I_c(\tau,\mathcal N)$ is achievable for classical messages with average error tending to zero. citations.exact_fact_text: [F1] [[thm-it-hsw-classical-quantum-channel-capacity]]: Holevo–Schumacher–Westmoreland capacity theorem for finite cq channels.
citations.quote:
Let $x\mapsto\rho_x$ be a finite-input, finite-output memoryless cq channel as in [[def-it-classical-quantum-memoryless-channel]]. With the average-error code convention of [[def-it-cq-channel-block-code-and-error]], its classical capacity in nats per use is
$$C_{\rm cq}=\max_{p\in\Delta(\mathcal X)}\chi_p,\qquad \chi_p:=S\!\left(\sum_xp_x\rho_x\right)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x).$$
For every $0\le R<C_{\rm cq}$ a sequence of codes with rate tending to $R$ has average error tending to zero, and every reliable sequence has limiting upper rate at most $C_{\rm cq}$. This theorem concerns a fixed finite classical input alphabet and does not assert a single-letter formula for general quantum-input channels.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F2] [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]]: Complementary channels and coherent information.
citations.quote:
Let $A$ and $B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\mathcal N:\mathcal L(A)\to\mathcal L(B)$ be a quantum channel as in [[def-qc-quantum-channel]]. Choose a finite-dimensional environment $E$ and a linear isometry $V:A\to B\otimes E$ such that

$$\mathcal N(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^*)$$

for every $X\in\mathcal L(A)$; such a dilation exists by [[thm-qc-finite-stinespring-dilation]]. The channel

$$\mathcal N^c(X):=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)\in\mathcal L(E)$$

is the **complementary channel associated with this chosen dilation**. The partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_B$ contracts the first factor of the ordered product $B\otimes E$ ([[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]).

It is a quantum channel: reorder $B\otimes E$ to $E\otimes B$ by the finite wire-permutation unitary ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]); the reordered $V$ is still an isometry, so tracing its second factor $B$ gives a channel by [[thm-qc-isometry-partial-trace-is-channel]].

For a density operator $\rho$ on $A$, choose a finite purification $|\psi\rangle\in A\otimes R$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_R|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|=\rho$ ([[def-qc-ensemble-and-purification]]), and define $\omega_{BR}:=(\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)$. Its **coherent information** from $A$ to $B$ is

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N):=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\omega_{BR}),$$

where $S$ is finite-dimensional von Neumann entropy in nats ([[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]). The value does not depend on the chosen purification: after padding reference spaces, any two purifications differ by a unitary on $R$ ([[thm-qc-purification-existence-and-unitary-equivalence]]); applying $\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R$ preserves that unitary relation. A unitary maps an orthonormal eigenbasis to an orthonormal eigenbasis with the same eigenvalues, so entropy is unchanged ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]). Padding adds only zero eigenvalues, which do not contribute.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F3] [[lem-it-quantum-coherent-information-complement-identity]]: Coherent information equals output entropy minus environment entropy.
citations.quote:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional channel, let $V:A\to B\otimes E$ be a finite Stinespring isometry, let $\mathcal N^c(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)$, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $A$. Then

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\mathcal N^c(\rho)).$$

The right-hand side is independent of the chosen Stinespring dilation, since it equals the purification-defined quantity in [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]].

citations.exact_fact_text: [F4] [[thm-qc-schmidt-decomposition]]: Schmidt decomposition.
citations.quote:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex-inner-product spaces with the tensor-product convention of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For every $\Psi\in H\otimes K$ there are an integer $r\ge0$, positive numbers $s_1,\ldots,s_r$, and orthonormal families $u_1,\ldots,u_r\in H$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_r\in K$ such that

$$\Psi=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j u_j\otimes v_j,\qquad \|\Psi\|^2=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j^2.$$

For $\Psi=0$ take $r=0$ and the empty sum. For any chosen ordered pair of orthonormal bases, the construction below obtains the $s_j$ as the positive singular values of the coefficient matrix of $\Psi$ in their ordered product basis.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F5] [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]: Ordered tensor registers, their inner product, and wire permutations.
citations.quote:
An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

citations.exact_fact_text: [F6] [[def-it-classical-quantum-state-and-holevo-information]]: the ensemble Holevo information is $S(\bar\rho)-\sum_xp_xS(\rho_x)$.
citations.quote:
Let $X$ be a finite nonempty classical label set, represented by a register $H_X$ with computational orthonormal basis $(\xi_x)_{x\in X}$ ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). For each $x$, write $\Pi_xz:=\langle z,\xi_x\rangle\xi_x$, the rank-one orthogonal projection using the root linear-first convention, as in [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Let $H_B$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A finite **classical-quantum state** is

$$\rho_{XB}:=\sum_{x\in X}p_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x,$$

where $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_xp_x=1$, and each $\rho_x$ is a density operator on $H_B$. It is a density operator by [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Its quantum marginal is $\bar\rho_B:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x=\operatorname{Tr}_X\rho_{XB}$ by the second-factor partial-trace formula in [[def-qc-partial-trace]], and it is a density operator by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. The **Holevo information** of this ensemble is

$$\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in X}):=S(\bar\rho_B)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x),$$

where zero-probability branches contribute nothing. This is measured in nats under [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

citations.exact_fact_text: [F9] [[lem-it-finite-weyl-twirl-partial-trace]]: the uniform finite Weyl conjugations on the second factor replace it by its maximally mixed state and retain the first-factor marginal, including dimension one.
citations.quote:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces with $d=\dim K\ge1$, and fix an ordered orthonormal basis $e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1}$ of $K$. Let $X e_j=e_{j+1\,\mathrm{mod}\,d}$ and $Z e_j=\omega^j e_j$, where $\omega=\exp(2\pi i/d)$ (and $\omega=1$ when $d=1$). For $R\in\operatorname{End}(H\otimes K)$,
$$\frac1{d^2}\sum_{p,q=0}^{d-1}(I_H\otimes X^pZ^q)R(I_H\otimes X^pZ^q)^\dagger=(\operatorname{Tr}_K R)\otimes I_K/d.$$

derivations.claim: Fix a $D$-dimensional subspace of the input, with embedding $J$ and flat state $\tau=JJ^*/D$. Share $|\Phi_D\rangle$ between the sender's subspace and a receiver reference $R$. On the sender half apply the $D^2$ Weyl unitaries, each uniformly likely, before the input embedding. The Weyl matrices in the fixed ordered basis are $U_{ab}|j\rangle=e^{2\pi i bj/D}|j+a\pmod D\rangle$. Reorder the shared state as $R\otimes\mathbb C^D$ using [F5]. Applying [F9] with retained factor $R$ and twirled factor the sender's $D$-dimensional register gives $I_R/D\otimes I_D/D$, since the retained marginal is $I_R/D$. Reordering back gives $I_D/D\otimes I_R/D$. The supplied finite root-of-unity calculation establishes the phase cancellation for every $D\ge1$.

Let $\sigma_{ab}$ be the joint output on $B R$ of this finite cq alphabet through $\mathcal N$. Because $(U_{ab}\otimes I)|\Phi_D\rangle=(I\otimes U_{ab}^T)|\Phi_D\rangle$ in coefficient coordinates, all $\sigma_{ab}$ are related by a unitary on $R$ and have identical entropy $S(\mathcal N^c(\tau))$ by purity of the full Stinespring output and [F4]. Their average is $\mathcal N(\tau)\otimes I_R/D$. The spectral theorem [F8] and logarithm law [F7] give $S(\mathcal N(\tau)\otimes I_R/D)=S(\mathcal N(\tau))+\ln D$. Thus [F6] gives the ensemble Holevo information exactly as $$\chi=\ln D+S(\mathcal N(\tau))-S(\mathcal N^c(\tau))=f_{\mathcal N}(\tau).$$ The HSW theorem applies to this fixed finite cq channel $ab\mapsto\sigma_{ab}$, with output $B R$. Each cq codeword is physically implemented by its sequence of Weyl operations on independent shared maximally entangled pairs. Its collective POVM is a permitted receiver measurement and its rate/error are exactly those of HSW. Therefore every nonnegative rate strictly below $f_{\mathcal N}(\tau)$ is entanglement-assisted achievable. Dimension $D=1$ is included: the one-letter ensemble then has Holevo information zero.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F6] [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]] and [[lem-it-finite-classical-kl-nonnegative-equality]]: $H(p)=-\sum_{p_i>0}p_i\ln p_i$, and $D(p\|q)\ge0$ for finite probability vectors.
citations.quote:
For a finite nonempty set identified with $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$, a **probability vector** is $p=(p_i)_{i=1}^k$ with $p_i\ge0$ and $\sum_i p_i=1$; it is the outcome-weight vector of a finite probability space ([[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]). Its Shannon entropy in natural units is
$$H(p):=-\sum_{i=1}^k p_i\ln p_i,$$
with $0\ln0:=0$. For probability vectors $p,q$ on the same set $[k]$, the relative entropy is
$$D(p\|q):=\sum_{i:p_i>0}p_i\ln(p_i/q_i),$$
with value $+\infty$ if $p_i>0=q_i$ for some $i$. A matrix $A\in[0,1]^{N\times m}$ is **row-stochastic** when each row sums to one. For a probability row vector $p$ on $[m]$ and a row vector $X\in[0,1]^m$, the dot product $pX^{\mathsf T}=\sum_{i=1}^m p_iX_i$ is the acceptance probability under distribution $p$.

These definitions use finite sets only; entropy is between $0$ and $\ln k$, as proved where needed below.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F6] [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]] and [[lem-it-finite-classical-kl-nonnegative-equality]]: $H(p)=-\sum_{p_i>0}p_i\ln p_i$, and $D(p\|q)\ge0$ for finite probability vectors.
citations.quote:
For probability vectors $p=(p_i)_{i\in I}$ and $q=(q_i)_{i\in I}$ on a finite nonempty set $I$, define

$$D(p\|q):=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\sum_{i:p_i>0}p_i\ln\frac{p_i}{q_i},&p_i>0\Rightarrow q_i>0,\\+\infty,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$

Then $D(p\|q)\ge0$, and $D(p\|q)=0$ if and only if $p=q$.

derivations.claim: Write $\rho=\sum_{j=1}^d\lambda_j|j\rangle\langle j|$, including zero eigenvalues. For each count vector $t=(n_1,\ldots,n_d)$ with $\sum_j n_j=n$, let $m_t$ be the number of product basis words of that type, $p_t=m_t\prod_{j:n_j>0}\lambda_j^{n_j}$ (zero if any such $\lambda_j=0$), and omit types with $p_t=0$. Let $P_t$ project onto the span of the words of type $t$ and set $\tau_t=P_t/m_t$. These states are flat, their supports are mutually orthogonal, and $$\rho^{\otimes n}=\sum_{t:p_t>0}p_t\tau_t.$$ There are at most $(n+1)^d$ types. If $N_T$ is their number and $u$ is the uniform law on them, [F6] gives $0\le D(p\|u)=\ln N_T-H(T)$, so $H(T)\le d\ln(n+1)$. Since $S(\tau_t)=\ln m_t$, the logarithm product law [F5] and $\sum_t p_t n_j=n\lambda_j$ yield $$\sum_t p_tS(\tau_t)=\sum_t p_t\ln m_t=nS(\rho)-H(T).$$

Let $B_t=\mathcal N^{\otimes n}(\tau_t)$ and $E_t=(\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\tau_t)$, with averages $\bar B=\sum_tp_tB_t=\mathcal N(\rho)^{\otimes n}$ and $\bar E=\sum_tp_tE_t=\mathcal N^c(\rho)^{\otimes n}$. By [F4], the receiver-minus-environment entropy identity applies to each type. The lower mixture bound [F1] gives $\sum_tp_tS(B_t)\ge S(\bar B)-H(T)$, while its upper bound gives $\sum_tp_tS(E_t)\le S(\bar E)$. Product spectral decompositions and [F5] give $S(\bar B)-S(\bar E)=n[S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\mathcal N^c(\rho))]=nI_c(\rho,\mathcal N)$. Hence $$\sum_tp_t I_c(\tau_t,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})\ge nI_c(\rho,\mathcal N)-H(T).$$ Adding $\sum_tp_tS(\tau_t)=nS(\rho)-H(T)$ from step 1.1 gives the second inequality.

Each displayed left side in step 2.1 is an average over the finite positive-probability types, so at least one type attains at least the corresponding average lower bound. These are exact finite-$n$ estimates; no replacement of fixed-dimensional continuity by a uniform bound is involved.

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a quantum channel between nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, and fix any finite Stinespring complement $\mathcal N^c:A\to E$. Both functions

$$\rho\longmapsto I_c(\rho,\mathcal N),\qquad \rho\longmapsto S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)$$

attain a maximum on the density operators on $A$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F1] [[def-qc-density-operator]], [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]], and [[cor-finite-dimensional-inner-product-spaces-have-orthonormal-bases]]: a state is a nonnegative trace-one self-adjoint operator with a finite orthonormal eigenbasis and nonnegative eigenvalues summing to one.
citations.quote:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$; non-negative and trace have the meanings of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]] and [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

citations.quote:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space and let
$T:V\to V$ be linear. The operator $T$ is **non-negative** when $T$ is
self-adjoint in the sense of [[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]] and

$$\langle Tv,v\rangle\ge 0$$

for every $v\in V$.

The operator $T$ is **positive** when $T$ is self-adjoint and

$$\langle Tv,v\rangle>0$$

for every nonzero $v\in V$.

Let $V,W$ be inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) over the same field and let $T:V\to W$ be linear ([[def-linear-map]]). An **adjoint** of $T$ is a linear map $T^*:W\to V$ such that

$$\langle Tv,w\rangle_W=\langle v,T^*w\rangle_V$$

for every $v\in V$ and $w\in W$. Existence is not part of the definition; in finite dimensions it will follow from Riesz representation.

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces. If $V=0$, define $\lVert T\rVert:=0$. If $V\ne0$, define the
**operator norm** of $T$ by

$$\lVert T\rVert:=\max\{\lVert Tv\rVert:\lVert v\rVert=1\}.$$

The next theorem proves that this maximum exists and equals the largest
singular value.

For vectors $u,v$ in a real or complex inner product space,

$$|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\lVert u\rVert\lVert v\rVert.$$

Equality holds if and only if $u$ and $v$ are linearly dependent, including the case in which either vector is zero.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F3] [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]] and [[lem-it-quantum-coherent-information-complement-identity]]: $I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\mathcal N^c(\rho))$.
citations.quote:
Let $A$ and $B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\mathcal N:\mathcal L(A)\to\mathcal L(B)$ be a quantum channel as in [[def-qc-quantum-channel]]. Choose a finite-dimensional environment $E$ and a linear isometry $V:A\to B\otimes E$ such that

$$\mathcal N(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^*)$$

for every $X\in\mathcal L(A)$; such a dilation exists by [[thm-qc-finite-stinespring-dilation]]. The channel

$$\mathcal N^c(X):=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)\in\mathcal L(E)$$

is the **complementary channel associated with this chosen dilation**. The partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_B$ contracts the first factor of the ordered product $B\otimes E$ ([[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]).

It is a quantum channel: reorder $B\otimes E$ to $E\otimes B$ by the finite wire-permutation unitary ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]); the reordered $V$ is still an isometry, so tracing its second factor $B$ gives a channel by [[thm-qc-isometry-partial-trace-is-channel]].

For a density operator $\rho$ on $A$, choose a finite purification $|\psi\rangle\in A\otimes R$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_R|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|=\rho$ ([[def-qc-ensemble-and-purification]]), and define $\omega_{BR}:=(\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)$. Its **coherent information** from $A$ to $B$ is

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N):=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\omega_{BR}),$$

where $S$ is finite-dimensional von Neumann entropy in nats ([[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]). The value does not depend on the chosen purification: after padding reference spaces, any two purifications differ by a unitary on $R$ ([[thm-qc-purification-existence-and-unitary-equivalence]]); applying $\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R$ preserves that unitary relation. A unitary maps an orthonormal eigenbasis to an orthonormal eigenbasis with the same eigenvalues, so entropy is unchanged ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]). Padding adds only zero eigenvalues, which do not contribute.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F3] [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]] and [[lem-it-quantum-coherent-information-complement-identity]]: $I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\mathcal N^c(\rho))$.
citations.quote:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional channel, let $V:A\to B\otimes E$ be a finite Stinespring isometry, let $\mathcal N^c(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)$, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $A$. Then

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\mathcal N^c(\rho)).$$

The right-hand side is independent of the chosen Stinespring dilation, since it equals the purification-defined quantity in [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]].

citations.exact_fact_text: [F4] [[lem-it-finite-quantum-entropy-continuity]]: entropy is continuous in operator norm on each fixed finite-dimensional state space, including at states with zero eigenvalues.
citations.quote: For each fixed finite dimension $d$, von Neumann entropy is continuous on density operators ([[def-qc-density-operator]]) on $\mathbb C^d$ in operator norm ([[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]]). Thus, if $\rho_k\to\rho$ in operator norm, then $S(\rho_k)\to S(\rho)$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F5] [[lem-euclidean-linear-maps-have-matrices-and-are-bounded]] and [[thm-all-norms-on-rn-are-equivalent]]: a linear map between finite-dimensional coordinate spaces is continuous, and the operator-norm topology agrees with the Euclidean coordinate topology.
citations.quote: For every linear $L:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n$ there is a unique matrix $A=(a_{ij})_{i<n,j<m}$ such that $(Lh)_i=\sum_{j<m}a_{ij}h_j$. Moreover there is $K\ge0$ with $\|Lh\|_2\le K\|h\|_2$ for every $h$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F5] [[lem-euclidean-linear-maps-have-matrices-and-are-bounded]] and [[thm-all-norms-on-rn-are-equivalent]]: a linear map between finite-dimensional coordinate spaces is continuous, and the operator-norm topology agrees with the Euclidean coordinate topology.
citations.quote:
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$. Then any two norms on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ are
equivalent ([[def-equivalent-norms]], [[def-norm-and-normed-space]]).

More precisely, for every norm $N$ on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ there are reals
$c > 0$ and $C' > 0$ with

$$c\,\lVert x\rVert_2 \;\le\; N(x) \;\le\; C'\,\lVert x\rVert_2 \qquad \text{for every } x \in \mathbb{R}^{n},$$

and the general statement follows because equivalence of norms is an equivalence
relation.

**Consequently all the metric notions on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ are norm independent**
for $n \ge 1$: any two norms give the same open sets, the same convergent
sequences with the same limits, the same Cauchy sequences and the same uniformly
continuous maps ([[def-equivalent-norms]]).

**The hypothesis $n \ge 1$ is used twice in the proof and both uses are marked**:
once so that the constant $C$ of
[[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]] exists, and once
so that the Euclidean unit sphere is **nonempty**, which is what the extreme
value theorem needs. At $n = 0$ the conclusion is true but vacuous, the zero
space carrying exactly one norm ([[def-norm-and-normed-space]]), and it is not
obtained from the argument below.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F6] [[thm-heine-borel-rn]]: a closed bounded subset of a positive-dimensional real Euclidean space is compact.
citations.quote:
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$, let $\mathbb{R}^n$ be the set of functions
$n \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $d_2$ be the Euclidean metric on it
([[lem-metrics-on-rn]]). Then:

1. **Closed boxes are compact.** For reals $a_k \le b_k$ $(k < n)$ the box
   $Q = \{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^n : a_k \le x_k \le b_k \text{ for every } k < n \,\}$
   is a compact subset of $(\mathbb{R}^n, d_2)$ ([[def-metric-compactness]]).
2. **Heine-Borel.** A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact subset of
   $(\mathbb{R}^n, d_2)$ if and only if $K$ is closed in $\mathbb{R}^n$
   ([[def-metric-topology]]) and bounded
   ([[def-metric-bounded-diameter]]).
3. **The real line.** A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a compact subset of
   $(\mathbb{R}, d_{\mathbb{R}})$, the usual metric $d_{\mathbb{R}}(x,y) = |x-y|$
   ([[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]]), if and only if $K$ is closed in
   $\mathbb{R}$ and bounded.

**No choice principle is used.** The bisection below halves one coordinate at a
time and takes the **left** half whenever the left half still fails to be finitely
covered, the right half otherwise: a rule with two outcomes, decided by a
property of the box, not a selection. That is the whole reason the theorem is
available in ZF, while the general "complete and totally bounded implies compact"
([[thm-complete-and-totally-bounded-implies-compact]]) is not.

The hypothesis $n \ge 1$ is inherited from [[lem-metrics-on-rn]], which defines
$\mathbb{R}^n$ and its metrics only there; the last remark below records what
happens at $n = 0$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F7] [[thm-extreme-value-metric]]: a continuous real-valued function on a nonempty compact metric space attains its maximum.
citations.quote:
Let $(X,d)$ be a nonempty compact metric space ([[def-metric-compactness]],
[[def-metric-space]]) and let $f : X \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous
([[def-metric-continuity]]), $\mathbb{R}$ carrying its usual metric
$d_{\mathbb{R}}(s,t) = |s-t|$ ([[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]]). Then the
image $f[X]$ is bounded above and below ([[def-bounded-set]]), and it has a
maximum and a minimum ([[def-max-min]]): there are points
$x_{\max}, x_{\min} \in X$ with

$$f(x_{\min}) \;\le\; f(x) \;\le\; f(x_{\max}) \qquad \text{for every } x \in X,$$

and then $f(x_{\max}) = \sup f[X]$ and $f(x_{\min}) = \inf f[X]$
([[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[def-infimum]]).

Nonemptiness of $X$ is a hypothesis and not an oversight: for $X = \emptyset$ the
image is empty and has neither a supremum nor a maximum. No choice principle is
used.

derivations.claim: Regard the self-adjoint endomorphisms of $A$ as a real vector space of dimension $d^2$, where $d=\dim A\ge1$, using an orthonormal basis of $A$ and the real diagonal and real/imaginary off-diagonal matrix coordinates. The state set is nonempty because $I_A/d$ is a state. It is closed: trace one and the self-adjoint matrix-coordinate equalities are closed conditions, and for each fixed $x\in A$, the quadratic form condition $\langle\rho x,x\rangle\ge0$ is closed by finite-dimensional continuity; [F1]–[F2] show their intersection is exactly the state set. It is bounded in the coordinate norm on Hermitian matrices: each eigenvalue lies in $[0,1]$, so the operator norm is at most one; for standard basis vectors $e_i,e_j$, [F2] gives $|\langle\rho e_j,e_i\rangle|\le1$, hence all $d^2$ real matrix coordinates are bounded. The operator and coordinate norms induce the same topology by [F5], so [F6] makes the state set compact in operator norm.

The channels $\mathcal N$ and $\mathcal N^c$ are finite-dimensional linear maps and hence continuous in operator norm by [F5]. Their outputs on states are states. By [F3]–[F4], $\rho\mapsto S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\mathcal N^c(\rho))$ is continuous; adding the continuous function $S(\rho)$ shows that the second displayed objective is continuous as well.
Apply [F7] to each of these two continuous real-valued functions on the nonempty compact state space from step 1.1. Each therefore attains its maximum, as asserted.

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional quantum channel, fix its complementary channel $\mathcal N^c:A\to E$, and let $\mathcal E=\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in\mathcal X}$ be a finite ensemble of density operators on $A$. Set $\bar\rho:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x$. Its **private information** is

$$I_p(\mathcal E,\mathcal N):=\chi(\{p_x,\mathcal N(\rho_x)\})-\chi(\{p_x,\mathcal N^c(\rho_x)\}),$$

where $\chi$ is the Holevo information from [[def-it-classical-quantum-state-and-holevo-information]]; zero-probability terms are omitted. Equivalently, it is the mutual information between the classical label and the receiver output minus that between the label and the complementary output.

citations.quote:
Let $X$ be a finite nonempty classical label set, represented by a register $H_X$ with computational orthonormal basis $(\xi_x)_{x\in X}$ ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). For each $x$, write $\Pi_xz:=\langle z,\xi_x\rangle\xi_x$, the rank-one orthogonal projection using the root linear-first convention, as in [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Let $H_B$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A finite **classical-quantum state** is

$$\rho_{XB}:=\sum_{x\in X}p_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x,$$

where $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_xp_x=1$, and each $\rho_x$ is a density operator on $H_B$. It is a density operator by [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Its quantum marginal is $\bar\rho_B:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x=\operatorname{Tr}_X\rho_{XB}$ by the second-factor partial-trace formula in [[def-qc-partial-trace]], and it is a density operator by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. The **Holevo information** of this ensemble is

$$\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in X}):=S(\bar\rho_B)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x),$$

where zero-probability branches contribute nothing. This is measured in nats under [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

derivations.claim: Apply [F3] to $\bar\rho$ and to every $\rho_x$ with $p_x>0$. Write $B_x=\mathcal N(\rho_x)$, $E_x=\mathcal N^c(\rho_x)$, $\bar B=\sum_xp_xB_x$, and $\bar E=\sum_xp_xE_x$. The difference of coherent informations becomes $S(\bar B)-S(\bar E)-\sum_xp_x(S(B_x)-S(E_x))$.

Regrouping the finite sums in step 1.1 gives $[S(\bar B)-\sum_xp_xS(B_x)]-[S(\bar E)-\sum_xp_xS(E_x)]$. Each bracket is the corresponding Holevo information by [F2], so their difference is $I_p(\mathcal E,\mathcal N)$ by [F1]. Terms with $p_x=0$ are absent in both sums.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F3] [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]: every finite-dimensional density operator has a finite orthonormal eigenbasis.
citations.quote:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F4] [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]: $\ln(xy)=\ln x+\ln y$ for positive $x,y$.
citations.quote:
The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,
$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

derivations.claim: Let $\tau$ and $\sigma$ be density operators with positive eigenvalues $(\lambda_i)_i$ and $(\mu_j)_j$, respectively. By [F3], the product eigenvectors form an orthonormal eigenbasis of $\tau\otimes\sigma$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_i\mu_j$; zero eigenvalues contribute zero. Expanding the entropy sum and using [F4], $\ln(\lambda_i\mu_j)=\ln\lambda_i+\ln\mu_j$, gives $S(\tau\otimes\sigma)=S(\tau)+S(\sigma)$.

Choose purifications $|\psi_i\rangle\in A_i\otimes R_i$ of $\rho_i$. Their product purifies $\rho_1\otimes\rho_2$. The joint output-reference states under the tensor-product channels and the complementary outputs under the product dilations are products. Applying step 1.1 to both entropy terms in [F1] proves the coherent-information equality.

The product ensemble has probabilities $p^{(1)}_{x_1}p^{(2)}_{x_2}$ and product receiver and environment output states. Its average receiver and environment states are the corresponding products of the two ensemble averages. Apply step 1.1 to each average and each positive-probability conditional state. Substitution into the two Holevo differences in [F2] separates the finite double sums into the two one-ensemble private-information terms, proving the second equality.
