source_export.quote:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional channel, let $V:A\to B\otimes E$ be a finite Stinespring isometry, let $\mathcal N^c(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)$, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $A$. Then

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\mathcal N^c(\rho)).$$

The right-hand side is independent of the chosen Stinespring dilation, since it equals the purification-defined quantity in [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]].

citations.exact_fact_text: [F1] [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]]: for a purification $|\psi\rangle\in A\otimes R$, $I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=S(\omega_B)-S(\omega_{BR})$, with $\omega_{BR}=(\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)$; the chosen complement is $\mathcal N^c(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)$.
citations.quote:
Let $A$ and $B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\mathcal N:\mathcal L(A)\to\mathcal L(B)$ be a quantum channel as in [[def-qc-quantum-channel]]. Choose a finite-dimensional environment $E$ and a linear isometry $V:A\to B\otimes E$ such that

$$\mathcal N(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^*)$$

for every $X\in\mathcal L(A)$; such a dilation exists by [[thm-qc-finite-stinespring-dilation]]. The channel

$$\mathcal N^c(X):=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)\in\mathcal L(E)$$

is the **complementary channel associated with this chosen dilation**. The partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_B$ contracts the first factor of the ordered product $B\otimes E$ ([[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]).

It is a quantum channel: reorder $B\otimes E$ to $E\otimes B$ by the finite wire-permutation unitary ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]); the reordered $V$ is still an isometry, so tracing its second factor $B$ gives a channel by [[thm-qc-isometry-partial-trace-is-channel]].

For a density operator $\rho$ on $A$, choose a finite purification $|\psi\rangle\in A\otimes R$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_R|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|=\rho$ ([[def-qc-ensemble-and-purification]]), and define $\omega_{BR}:=(\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)$. Its **coherent information** from $A$ to $B$ is

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N):=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\omega_{BR}),$$

where $S$ is finite-dimensional von Neumann entropy in nats ([[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]). The value does not depend on the chosen purification: after padding reference spaces, any two purifications differ by a unitary on $R$ ([[thm-qc-purification-existence-and-unitary-equivalence]]); applying $\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R$ preserves that unitary relation. A unitary maps an orthonormal eigenbasis to an orthonormal eigenbasis with the same eigenvalues, so entropy is unchanged ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]). Padding adds only zero eigenvalues, which do not contribute.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F2] [[def-qc-ensemble-and-purification]] and [[thm-qc-purification-existence-and-unitary-equivalence]]: a purification is a unit vector $|\psi\rangle\in A\otimes R$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_R|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|=\rho$, and such a finite purification exists.
citations.quote:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space. A **finite ensemble of density operators** on $H$ is a positive integer $n$, weights $p_1,\ldots,p_n\ge0$ with $\sum_{a=1}^np_a=1$, and density operators $\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_n$ on $H$. Its **barycenter** is $\bar\rho=\sum_{a=1}^np_a\rho_a$. A zero-weight component still names a density operator but contributes zero to the barycenter.

Let $K$ be any finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space. A **purification** of a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ is a unit vector $\Psi\in H\otimes K$ such that

$$\operatorname{Tr}_K(|\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|)=\rho.$$

The tensor factors are ordered $H$ then $K$. Tensor products, outer products and partial trace have the conventions of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]] and [[def-qc-partial-trace]]. The auxiliary space may be any finite dimension that supports such a unit vector.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F2] [[def-qc-ensemble-and-purification]] and [[thm-qc-purification-existence-and-unitary-equivalence]]: a purification is a unit vector $|\psi\rangle\in A\otimes R$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_R|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|=\rho$, and such a finite purification exists.
citations.quote:
Every density operator $\rho$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space $H$ has a purification on some finite-dimensional auxiliary space. More precisely, if $r=\operatorname{rank}(\rho)$, it has one on an auxiliary space of dimension $r$. If $\Psi_i\in H\otimes K_i$ ($i=1,2$) are any two purifications of the same $\rho$, then for every integer $m\ge\max(\dim K_1,\dim K_2)$ and every pair of linear isometric embeddings $\iota_i:K_i\to\mathbb C^m$, where $\mathbb C^m$ has its standard complex inner product, there is a unitary $U$ on $\mathbb C^m$ such that

$$ (I_H\otimes U)(I_H\otimes\iota_2)\Psi_2=(I_H\otimes\iota_1)\Psi_1. $$

citations.exact_fact_text: [F3] [[thm-qc-schmidt-decomposition]]: a finite pure bipartite vector has a Schmidt decomposition, so its two reduced density operators have the same positive eigenvalues with multiplicities.
citations.quote:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex-inner-product spaces with the tensor-product convention of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For every $\Psi\in H\otimes K$ there are an integer $r\ge0$, positive numbers $s_1,\ldots,s_r$, and orthonormal families $u_1,\ldots,u_r\in H$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_r\in K$ such that

$$\Psi=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j u_j\otimes v_j,\qquad \|\Psi\|^2=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j^2.$$

For $\Psi=0$ take $r=0$ and the empty sum. For any chosen ordered pair of orthonormal bases, the construction below obtains the $s_j$ as the positive singular values of the coefficient matrix of $\Psi$ in their ordered product basis.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F4] [[thm-qc-finite-stinespring-dilation]]: $\mathcal N(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^*)$ for every input operator $X$.
citations.quote:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be a quantum channel. It has a finite
Kraus representation, and for any chosen such representation with $N$
operators $K_a:H\to K$ there are an $N$-dimensional environment $E$ and a
linear isometry $V:H\to K\otimes E$ such that
$$\Phi(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^\dagger)\quad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H).$$

citations.exact_fact_text: [F5] [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]: $S(\tau)=-\sum_{\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j$ for the eigenvalues of a finite-dimensional density operator; zero eigenvalues contribute zero.
citations.quote:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F6] [[def-qc-partial-trace]], [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]], [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], and [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]: ordered partial traces sum equal traced-factor indices; the factors of $B\otimes E\otimes R$ can be reordered by a unitary wire permutation.
citations.quote:
For a complex vector space $H$, write $\operatorname{End}(H)$ for the set of
linear maps $H\to H$ ([[def-linear-map]]).

Let $H_A,H_B$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces with fixed
ordered orthonormal bases $(e_i)_{i<a}$ and $(f_j)_{j<b}$, respectively. The
ordered product basis of $H_A\otimes H_B$ has the $A$ index first. For
$R\in\operatorname{End}(H_A\otimes H_B)$ define
$\operatorname{Tr}_B(R)\in\operatorname{End}(H_A)$ by

$$\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_B(R)\bigr)_{i i'}:=\sum_{j<b}R_{(i,j),(i',j)}.$$

Rows are output coordinates and columns are input coordinates, as in
[[def-coordinate-column-and-matrix-of-a-linear-map]]. If $b=0$, the sum is
empty and equals $0$. The notation $\operatorname{Tr}_B$ means that the second
factor is contracted; the first factor and its order are retained.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F6] [[def-qc-partial-trace]], [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]], [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], and [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]: ordered partial traces sum equal traced-factor indices; the factors of $B\otimes E\otimes R$ can be reordered by a unitary wire permutation.
citations.quote:
Let $H_G,H_Q$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, and fix
the factor order $H_G\otimes H_Q$. For ordered orthonormal bases
$(g_s)$ and $(q_\alpha)$, define
$$\operatorname{Tr}_G:\mathcal B(H_G\otimes H_Q)\to\mathcal B(H_Q),\qquad (\operatorname{Tr}_G X)_{\alpha\beta}=\sum_sX_{(s,\alpha),(s,\beta)},$$
where $X_{(s,\alpha),(t,\beta)}=\langle X(g_t\otimes q_\beta),
g_s\otimes q_\alpha\rangle$ under the linear-first convention. Equivalently,
this is the partial trace over the second factor after swapping the two wires.
The partial-trace characterization and wire-permutation unitarity in
[[thm-qc-partial-trace-characterization-and-basis-independence]] and
[[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]] show that the map is independent of
the chosen orthonormal bases. In particular, the same definition applies when
$H_Q=H_L\otimes H_R$, with that residual factor order left unchanged. For an
operator on $(H_G\otimes H_L)\otimes H_R$, use the canonical associator of
the ordered tensor-register construction to view it on
$H_G\otimes(H_L\otimes H_R)$ before taking this partial trace.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F6] [[def-qc-partial-trace]], [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]], [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], and [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]: ordered partial traces sum equal traced-factor indices; the factors of $B\otimes E\otimes R$ can be reordered by a unitary wire permutation.
citations.quote:
An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

citations.exact_fact_text: [F6] [[def-qc-partial-trace]], [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]], [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], and [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]: ordered partial traces sum equal traced-factor indices; the factors of $B\otimes E\otimes R$ can be reordered by a unitary wire permutation.
citations.quote:
Let $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$ be a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces, with the product bases of
[[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For a permutation $\sigma$ of the
factor positions, the map $P_\sigma$ that reorders the factors is a bijective
linear isometry from $H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$ to
$H_{\sigma(0)}\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{\sigma(n-1)}$. When source and target
are identified as the same register, $P_\sigma$ is a unitary operator in the
sense of [[def-linear-isometry-and-orthogonal-or-unitary-operator]].

derivations.claim: Choose a finite purification $|\psi\rangle\in A\otimes R$ of $\rho$ using [F2], and put $|\Omega\rangle=(V\otimes I_R)|\psi\rangle\in B\otimes E\otimes R$. Since $V$ is an isometry, $|\Omega\rangle$ is a unit vector. Reorder to $B\otimes R\otimes E$ using [F6]; tracing $E$ gives $\omega_{BR}$ because [F4] says $\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^*)=\mathcal N(X)$. Tracing $B$ and $R$ gives $\operatorname{Tr}_B(V\rho V^*)=\mathcal N^c(\rho)$: in the ordered product basis, the two finite partial-trace sums contract the $R$ index to $\operatorname{Tr}_R|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|=\rho$ and then contract the $B$ index.

Regard the reordered $|\Omega\rangle$ as a bipartite vector across $(B\otimes R)|E$. By [F3], the positive eigenvalues of its $BR$ and $E$ marginals coincide. The entropy formula [F5] therefore gives $S(\omega_{BR})=S(\mathcal N^c(\rho))$. Substitute this identity into [F1] to obtain the displayed formula. As the left side of the formula is independent of both the purification and the chosen complement, the right side has the same value for every finite dilation.

source_export.quote:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space of dimension $d$, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$. Then

$$S(\rho)\le\ln d,$$

with equality if and only if $\rho=I_H/d$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F1] [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]: $S(\rho)=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho)$, with zero-eigenvalue terms omitted.
citations.quote:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F2] [[def-it-finite-dimensional-quantum-relative-entropy]]: on support inclusion, $D(A\|B)=\operatorname{tr}(A\ln A)-\operatorname{tr}(A\ln B)$.
citations.quote:
Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $A,B:H\to H$ be non-negative operators. For such an operator $A$, set $\operatorname{supp}(A):=(\ker A)^\perp$, where $\ker A$ is the kernel of a linear map ([[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]); this extends the density-operator support convention in [[def-qc-density-operator]]. If $\operatorname{supp}(A)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(B)$, define

$$D(A\|B):=\operatorname{tr}(A\ln A)-\operatorname{tr}(A\ln B).$$

Here $\ln A$ is defined spectrally on the positive eigenspaces of $A$ with $0\ln0:=0$, and $\ln B$ in the cross term is restricted to $\operatorname{supp}(B)$; the support condition ensures that $A$ vanishes on $\ker B$, so the omitted kernel contributes zero. If $\operatorname{supp}(A)\nsubseteq\operatorname{supp}(B)$, set $D(A\|B):=+\infty$. In particular, $D(0\|B)=0$. For density operators this is the finite-dimensional **quantum relative entropy**. The logarithms are natural, so the value is in nats; the base-two value is $D_2(A\|B):=D(A\|B)/\ln2$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F3] [[thm-it-quantum-relative-entropy-nonnegative-equality]]: for finite-dimensional density operators $\rho,\sigma$, $D(\rho\|\sigma)\ge0$, with equality exactly when $\rho=\sigma$.
citations.quote:
For density operators $\rho,\sigma$ on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space,

$$D(\rho\|\sigma)\ge0,$$

with equality if and only if $\rho=\sigma$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F4] [[def-qc-density-operator]] and [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]: states are nonnegative trace-one operators and have finite orthonormal eigenbases.
citations.quote:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$; non-negative and trace have the meanings of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]] and [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F4] [[def-qc-density-operator]] and [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]: states are nonnegative trace-one operators and have finite orthonormal eigenbases.
citations.quote:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F5] [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]: the trace of $I_H$ is $d$ and the trace is linear.
citations.quote:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F6] [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]: $\ln(1/d)=-\ln d$ for $d>0$.
citations.quote:
The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,
$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

derivations.claim: The operator $\tau:=I_H/d$ is a density operator: it is nonnegative and has trace $d/d=1$ by [F4]–[F5]. Its support is all of $H$, so $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(\tau)$ and the finite formula in [F2] applies.

Spectral calculus gives $\ln\tau=\ln(1/d)I_H=-(\ln d)I_H$ by [F4], [F6]. Hence [F1]–[F2] yield $D(\rho\|\tau)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho)-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\tau)=-S(\rho)+\ln d$, using $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$ by [F4]. By [F3], this is nonnegative, so $S(\rho)\le\ln d$.
Equality $S(\rho)=\ln d$ is equivalent by step 2.1 to $D(\rho\|\tau)=0$. The equality case of [F3] then gives $\rho=\tau=I_H/d$. Conversely, substituting $\rho=I_H/d$ into [F1] gives $S(\rho)=\ln d$.

source_export.quote:
Let $\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon}$ be the finite-dimensional erasure channel with data dimension $d\ge1$ and erasure probability $\epsilon\in[0,1]$, with the complementary dilation in [[lem-it-qudit-erasure-channel-complement-and-degradability]]. For every input state $\rho$,

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon})=(1-2\epsilon)S(\rho).$$

citations.exact_fact_text: [F1] [[lem-it-qudit-erasure-channel-complement-and-degradability]]: the receiver state is $(1-\epsilon)\rho\oplus\epsilon|e_B\rangle\langle e_B|$ and the complementary state is $\epsilon\rho\oplus(1-\epsilon)|e_E\rangle\langle e_E|$ under the declared data-flag identifications.
citations.quote:
For $\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon}$, choose the Stinespring isometry in [[thm-it-qudit-erasure-channel-is-cptp]], with environment $E=A\oplus\mathbb C e_E$. Its complement is

$$\mathcal E^c_{d,\epsilon}(X)=\epsilon J_EXJ_E^*\oplus(1-\epsilon)\operatorname{tr}(X)|e_E\rangle\langle e_E|.$$

The channel is degradable for $0\le\epsilon\le\tfrac12$ and antidegradable for $\tfrac12\le\epsilon\le1$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F2] [[lem-it-quantum-coherent-information-complement-identity]]: $I_c(\rho,\mathcal E)=S(\mathcal E(\rho))-S(\mathcal E^c(\rho))$.
citations.quote:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional channel, let $V:A\to B\otimes E$ be a finite Stinespring isometry, let $\mathcal N^c(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)$, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $A$. Then

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\mathcal N^c(\rho)).$$

The right-hand side is independent of the chosen Stinespring dilation, since it equals the purification-defined quantity in [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]].

citations.exact_fact_text: [F3] [[lem-it-flagged-state-entropy-formula]]: $S(p\rho\oplus(1-p)|e\rangle\langle e|)=h(p)+pS(\rho)$, including $p=0,1$.
citations.quote:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $\tau$ be a density operator on $H$, let $e$ be a unit vector orthogonal to the data summand in $H\oplus\mathbb C e$, and let $p\in[0,1]$. With $h(p):=-p\ln p-(1-p)\ln(1-p)$ and $0\ln0:=0$, the block-diagonal state

$$\omega_p:=p\tau\oplus(1-p)|e\rangle\langle e|$$

satisfies $S(\omega_p)=h(p)+pS(\tau)$.

derivations.claim: Apply [F3] to the two states in [F1]. Their entropies are $h(\epsilon)+(1-\epsilon)S(\rho)$ and $h(1-\epsilon)+\epsilon S(\rho)$, respectively. By the definition of $h$ and the logarithm product and reciprocal laws in [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]], $h(1-\epsilon)=h(\epsilon)$, including the endpoint convention $0\ln0=0$.

Subtract the complementary-output entropy from the receiver-output entropy as in [F2]. The equal binary-entropy terms from step 1.1 cancel, leaving $(1-2\epsilon)S(\rho)$. The derivation is valid at $\epsilon=0,1$ by [F3], so no open-interval restriction is needed.

source_export.quote:
For $\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon}$, choose the Stinespring isometry in [[thm-it-qudit-erasure-channel-is-cptp]], with environment $E=A\oplus\mathbb C e_E$. Its complement is

$$\mathcal E^c_{d,\epsilon}(X)=\epsilon J_EXJ_E^*\oplus(1-\epsilon)\operatorname{tr}(X)|e_E\rangle\langle e_E|.$$

The channel is degradable for $0\le\epsilon\le\tfrac12$ and antidegradable for $\tfrac12\le\epsilon\le1$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F1] [[def-it-qudit-erasure-channel]]: the receiver output space is the orthogonal sum of the data space and its erasure flag, and the data map is the isometric inclusion $J_B$.
citations.quote:
Let $A$ be a $d$-dimensional complex inner-product space with $d\ge1$. Form the orthogonal direct sum $B:=A\oplus\mathbb C e$, where $e$ is a unit erasure vector orthogonal to every vector in $A$; the inner product on pairs is $\langle(x,a),(y,b)\rangle_B=\langle x,y\rangle_A+a\overline b$. Thus $\dim B=d+1$ by [[cor-dimension-of-a-direct-sum]]. Let $J:A\to B$ be the isometric inclusion into the data summand.

For an erasure probability $\epsilon\in[0,1]$, the **$d$-dimensional quantum erasure channel** is the linear map

$$\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon}(X):=(1-\epsilon)JXJ^*\oplus \epsilon\operatorname{tr}(X)|e\rangle\langle e|,\qquad X\in\mathcal L(A).$$

For a density operator $\rho$, this outputs the data state with probability $1-\epsilon$ and the orthogonal erasure flag with probability $\epsilon$. The definition is on the full operator space, and its channel property is established in [[thm-it-qudit-erasure-channel-is-cptp]].

citations.exact_fact_text: [F2] [[def-it-degradable-channel]]: degradability means that a channel from $B$ to $E$ simulates the complement, and antidegradability means a channel from $E$ to $B$ simulates the original channel.
citations.quote:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional channel and fix a complementary channel $\mathcal N^c:A\to E$ coming from one finite Stinespring isometry. Relative to this chosen dilation, $\mathcal N$ is **degradable** if there exists a quantum channel $\mathcal D:B\to E$ such that

$$\mathcal N^c=\mathcal D\circ\mathcal N.$$

It is **antidegradable** relative to this dilation if there exists a quantum channel $\mathcal A:E\to B$ such that

$$\mathcal N=\mathcal A\circ\mathcal N^c.$$

All hypotheses and conclusions below use the same fixed complementary dilation and the corresponding degrading or antidegrading channel.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F3] [[thm-it-qudit-erasure-channel-is-cptp]]: $\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon}$ is a finite-dimensional channel.
citations.quote: For every integer $d\ge1$ and $\epsilon\in[0,1]$, the map $\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon}$ defined in [[def-it-qudit-erasure-channel]] is a finite-dimensional quantum channel.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F4] [[thm-qc-kraus-map-completely-positive]]: every finite Kraus sum is completely positive.
citations.quote:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ have a finite Kraus representation
$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a\in A}K_a X K_a^\dagger$. Then $\Phi$ is completely positive.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F5] [[thm-qc-trace-preserving-kraus-normalization]]: a finite Kraus sum is trace-preserving when the sum of $K_j^*K_j$ is the identity.
citations.quote:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let
$\Phi(X)=\sum_{a\in A}K_aXK_a^\dagger$ be a finite Kraus representation,
where each $K_a:H\to K$. The map $\Phi$ is trace-preserving on all of
$\mathcal L(H)$, meaning $\operatorname{tr}_K(\Phi(X))=\operatorname{tr}_H(X)$
for every $X\in\mathcal L(H)$, if and only if
$$\sum_{a\in A}K_a^\dagger K_a=I_H.$$

citations.exact_fact_text: [F6] [[def-qc-quantum-channel]]: a channel is complex-linear, completely positive, and trace-preserving.
citations.quote:
Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces. A
**quantum channel** from $H$ to $K$ is a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ ([[def-linear-map]]) that is completely
positive ([[def-qc-completely-positive-map]]) and trace-preserving, meaning

$$\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(X))=\operatorname{tr}(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

where trace is the basis-independent trace of a finite-dimensional
endomorphism ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]). Trace preservation is
required on the full operator space, not only on density operators. This
definition is mathematical and assumes no physical realization.

derivations.claim: Use the isometry $V_\epsilon x=\sqrt{1-\epsilon}J_Bx\otimes e_E+\sqrt\epsilon e\otimes J_Ex$ from the proof of [[thm-it-qudit-erasure-channel-is-cptp]]. Tracing the first factor $B$ leaves the data block $\epsilon J_EXJ_E^*$ and the flag block $(1-\epsilon)\operatorname{tr}(X)|e_E\rangle\langle e_E|$; the cross terms vanish because the data and erasure subspaces are orthogonal. The data block precedes the flag block because $E=A\oplus\mathbb C e_E$.

Suppose $0\le\epsilon\le\tfrac12$ and set $\alpha=\epsilon/(1-\epsilon)\in[0,1]$. Choose an orthonormal basis $(u_j)_{j<d}$ of the data summand of $B$, and define the finite Kraus family from $B$ to $E$ by $K_0=\sqrt\alpha J_EJ_B^*$, $K_j=\sqrt{1-\alpha}|e_E\rangle\langle u_j|$ for $j<d$, and $K_e=|e_E\rangle\langle e_B|$. The sum of adjoint products is $\alpha\Pi_A+(1-\alpha)\Pi_A+|e_B\rangle\langle e_B|=I_B$, so the induced map $\mathcal D_\epsilon(X)=\sum KXK^*$ is a channel by [F4]–[F6]. On an erasure-channel output, its data block has weight $\alpha(1-\epsilon)X=\epsilon X$ and its flag block has weight $[(1-\alpha)(1-\epsilon)+\epsilon]\operatorname{tr}(X)=(1-\epsilon)\operatorname{tr}(X)$. Thus $\mathcal D_\epsilon\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon}=\mathcal E^c_{d,\epsilon}$, proving degradability.

Suppose $\tfrac12\le\epsilon\le1$ and set $\beta=(1-\epsilon)/\epsilon\in[0,1]$. Choose an orthonormal basis $(u_j^E)_{j<d}$ of the data summand of $E$ and define a finite Kraus family from $E$ to $B$ by $L_0=\sqrt\beta J_BJ_E^*$, $L_j=\sqrt{1-\beta}|e_B\rangle\langle u_j^E|$ for $j<d$, and $L_e=|e_B\rangle\langle e_E|$. Its adjoint products sum to $I_E$, so its Kraus map $\mathcal A_\epsilon$ is a channel by [F4]–[F6]. Applying it to the complement in step 1.1 gives data weight $\beta\epsilon X=(1-\epsilon)X$ and erasure-flag weight $[(1-\beta)\epsilon+(1-\epsilon)]\operatorname{tr}(X)=\epsilon\operatorname{tr}(X)$. Hence $\mathcal A_\epsilon\mathcal E^c_{d,\epsilon}=\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon}$, proving antidegradability. At $\epsilon=\tfrac12$ both parameters equal one and both relations hold.

source_export.quote:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional degradable channel with a fixed complement $\mathcal N^c$. Then

$$Q(\mathcal N)=P(\mathcal N)=\max_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A)}I_c(\rho,\mathcal N),$$

and both regularizations in the quantum and private capacity formulas collapse to this one-use maximum.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F1] [[def-it-degradable-channel]]: a degrading channel $\mathcal D:B\to E$ satisfies $\mathcal N^c=\mathcal D\circ\mathcal N$.
citations.quote:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional channel and fix a complementary channel $\mathcal N^c:A\to E$ coming from one finite Stinespring isometry. Relative to this chosen dilation, $\mathcal N$ is **degradable** if there exists a quantum channel $\mathcal D:B\to E$ such that

$$\mathcal N^c=\mathcal D\circ\mathcal N.$$

It is **antidegradable** relative to this dilation if there exists a quantum channel $\mathcal A:E\to B$ such that

$$\mathcal N=\mathcal A\circ\mathcal N^c.$$

All hypotheses and conclusions below use the same fixed complementary dilation and the corresponding degrading or antidegrading channel.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F2] [[lem-it-degradable-channel-coherent-information-concavity-and-subadditivity]]: for a degradable channel, coherent information is concave and nonnegative; for product degradable channels it is subadditive on joint inputs and its optimized value is additive.
citations.quote:
Let $\mathcal N_i:A_i\to B_i$ for $i=1,2$ be finite-dimensional degradable channels with complements $\mathcal N_i^c=\mathcal D_i\circ\mathcal N_i$. Then $\rho\mapsto I_c(\rho,\mathcal N_i)$ is concave and nonnegative. For every joint input state $\rho_{A_1A_2}$,

$$I_c(\rho_{A_1A_2},\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2)\le I_c(\rho_{A_1},\mathcal N_1)+I_c(\rho_{A_2},\mathcal N_2).$$

Consequently the supremum coherent information of $\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2$ is the sum of the two single-channel suprema.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F3] [[lem-it-maximum-coherent-information-attained]]: the finite-dimensional coherent information maximum is attained.
citations.quote:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a quantum channel between nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, and fix any finite Stinespring complement $\mathcal N^c:A\to E$. Both functions

$$\rho\longmapsto I_c(\rho,\mathcal N),\qquad \rho\longmapsto S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)$$

attain a maximum on the density operators on $A$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F4] [[thm-it-quantum-channel-capacity-regularized-coherent-information]] and [[thm-it-quantum-channel-capacity-regularized-private-information]]: the general capacities equal their regularized coherent-information and private-information sequences, respectively.
citations.quote:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional memoryless quantum channel. For $n\ge1$, put

$$q_n(\mathcal N):=\sup_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A^{\otimes n})}I_c(\rho,\mathcal N^{\otimes n}).$$

Under the subspace entanglement-transmission convention in [[def-it-quantum-channel-operational-capacities]],

$$Q(\mathcal N)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{q_n(\mathcal N)}n=\sup_{n\ge1}\frac{q_n(\mathcal N)}n.$$

No general single-letter or additivity assertion is made.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F4] [[thm-it-quantum-channel-capacity-regularized-coherent-information]] and [[thm-it-quantum-channel-capacity-regularized-private-information]]: the general capacities equal their regularized coherent-information and private-information sequences, respectively.
citations.quote:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional memoryless quantum channel. For each $n\ge1$, let

$$p_n(\mathcal N):=\sup_{\mathcal E_n} I_p(\mathcal E_n,\mathcal N^{\otimes n}),$$

where the supremum ranges over all finite ensembles of input states on $A^{\otimes n}$. Under the strong-secrecy, average-error convention in [[def-it-quantum-channel-operational-capacities]],

$$P(\mathcal N)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{p_n(\mathcal N)}n=\sup_{n\ge1}\frac{p_n(\mathcal N)}n.$$

This statement is regularized and asserts no general single-letter formula.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F5] [[lem-it-private-information-is-coherent-information-difference]]: for an ensemble $\{p_x,\rho_x\}$, $I_p=I_c(\bar\rho,\mathcal N)-\sum_xp_xI_c(\rho_x,\mathcal N)$.
citations.quote:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional channel with chosen complement $\mathcal N^c:A\to E$, and let $\mathcal E=\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in\mathcal X}$ be a finite ensemble on $A$ with $\bar\rho=\sum_xp_x\rho_x$. Then

$$I_p(\mathcal E,\mathcal N)=I_c(\bar\rho,\mathcal N)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_x I_c(\rho_x,\mathcal N).$$

citations.exact_fact_text: [F6] [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]: each density operator is a finite convex combination of rank-one eigenprojections.
citations.quote:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

derivations.claim: The tensor power of a degradable channel is degradable: the product degrading map $\mathcal D^{\otimes n}$ is a channel by [[thm-qc-channels-compose-and-tensor]], and it maps $(\mathcal N^{\otimes n})(\rho)$ to $(\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho)$. Therefore [F2] gives $\sup_\rho I_c(\rho,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})=n\max_\rho I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)$. Substituting in the regularized quantum formula [F4] yields $Q(\mathcal N)=\max_\rho I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)$.

For any $n$-use input ensemble $\{p_x,\rho_x\}$, its tensor-power channel is degradable by step 1.1. By [F5], its private information is the coherent information of the average minus the average branch coherent information. Each branch term is nonnegative by [F2], so this private information is at most $I_c(\bar\rho,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})\le n\max_\rho I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)$. Hence the $n$-use private-information supremum has the same upper bound.

Choose a maximizing state $\rho_*$ using [F3], and decompose it spectrally as $\rho_* =\sum_jp_j|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|$ using [F6]. For a pure input $|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|$, choose a one-dimensional purification reference; the joint output-reference state has the same nonzero eigenvalues as $\mathcal N(|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|)$, so the defining formula in [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]] gives $I_c(|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|,\mathcal N)=0$. Therefore the pure-state ensemble has private information $I_c(\rho_*,\mathcal N)$ by [F5]. Thus $p_1\ge\max_\rho I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)$; step 2.1 with $n=1$ gives the reverse inequality, and step 2.1 for all $n$ gives $p_n/n\le\max_\rho I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)$. The regularized formula [F4] therefore yields $P(\mathcal N)=\max_\rho I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)$.
The identities in steps 1.1 and 3.1 prove the stated equality and remove both regularizations.

source_export.quote:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional quantum channel. Under the shared-entanglement coding convention in [[def-it-quantum-channel-operational-capacities]],

$$C_E(\mathcal N)=\max_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A)}\bigl(S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)\bigr)=\max_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A)}I(R;B)_{(\operatorname{id}_R\otimes\mathcal N)(\psi_\rho)},$$

where $\psi_\rho$ is any finite purification of $\rho$ on $R\otimes A$. The value is additive: $C_E(\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2)=C_E(\mathcal N_1)+C_E(\mathcal N_2)$ for finite-dimensional channels.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F1] [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]], [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]], and [[thm-qc-schmidt-decomposition]]: for a purification $\psi_{RA}$, $I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=S(B)-S(RB)$ and $S(R)=S(\rho)$.
citations.quote:
Let $A$ and $B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\mathcal N:\mathcal L(A)\to\mathcal L(B)$ be a quantum channel as in [[def-qc-quantum-channel]]. Choose a finite-dimensional environment $E$ and a linear isometry $V:A\to B\otimes E$ such that

$$\mathcal N(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^*)$$

for every $X\in\mathcal L(A)$; such a dilation exists by [[thm-qc-finite-stinespring-dilation]]. The channel

$$\mathcal N^c(X):=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)\in\mathcal L(E)$$

is the **complementary channel associated with this chosen dilation**. The partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_B$ contracts the first factor of the ordered product $B\otimes E$ ([[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]).

It is a quantum channel: reorder $B\otimes E$ to $E\otimes B$ by the finite wire-permutation unitary ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]); the reordered $V$ is still an isometry, so tracing its second factor $B$ gives a channel by [[thm-qc-isometry-partial-trace-is-channel]].

For a density operator $\rho$ on $A$, choose a finite purification $|\psi\rangle\in A\otimes R$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_R|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|=\rho$ ([[def-qc-ensemble-and-purification]]), and define $\omega_{BR}:=(\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)$. Its **coherent information** from $A$ to $B$ is

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N):=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\omega_{BR}),$$

where $S$ is finite-dimensional von Neumann entropy in nats ([[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]). The value does not depend on the chosen purification: after padding reference spaces, any two purifications differ by a unitary on $R$ ([[thm-qc-purification-existence-and-unitary-equivalence]]); applying $\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R$ preserves that unitary relation. A unitary maps an orthonormal eigenbasis to an orthonormal eigenbasis with the same eigenvalues, so entropy is unchanged ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]). Padding adds only zero eigenvalues, which do not contribute.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F1] [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]], [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]], and [[thm-qc-schmidt-decomposition]]: for a purification $\psi_{RA}$, $I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=S(B)-S(RB)$ and $S(R)=S(\rho)$.
citations.quote:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F1] [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]], [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]], and [[thm-qc-schmidt-decomposition]]: for a purification $\psi_{RA}$, $I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=S(B)-S(RB)$ and $S(R)=S(\rho)$.
citations.quote:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex-inner-product spaces with the tensor-product convention of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For every $\Psi\in H\otimes K$ there are an integer $r\ge0$, positive numbers $s_1,\ldots,s_r$, and orthonormal families $u_1,\ldots,u_r\in H$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_r\in K$ such that

$$\Psi=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j u_j\otimes v_j,\qquad \|\Psi\|^2=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j^2.$$

For $\Psi=0$ take $r=0$ and the empty sum. For any chosen ordered pair of orthonormal bases, the construction below obtains the $s_j$ as the positive singular values of the coefficient matrix of $\Psi$ in their ordered product basis.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F2] [[def-it-finite-quantum-information-measures]]: $I(R;B)=S(R)+S(B)-S(RB)$.
citations.quote:
For a finite bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B$, write $\rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho_{AB}$ and $\rho_B=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$, using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]] and [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]. They are states by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. Define

$$S(A)_\rho:=S(\rho_A),\qquad S(A\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})-S(\rho_B),\qquad I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a finite tripartite state $\rho_{ABC}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, set $\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_C}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying the factors as $(H_A\otimes H_B)\otimes H_C$, and $\rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_A}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying them as $H_A\otimes(H_B\otimes H_C)$. Let $P:H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C\to H_A\otimes H_C\otimes H_B$ be the wire permutation taking factor order $A,B,C$ to $A,C,B$ ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]) whose unique adjoint $P^*$ exists by [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]], and set $\rho_{AC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}(P\rho_{ABC}P^*)$, tracing out the last factor. Because $P$ is unitary, $P\rho_{ABC}P^*$ is a state: unitary conjugation preserves non-negativity by the adjoint identity ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]) and preserves trace by cyclicity ([[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]). Finally set $\rho_C:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\rho_{BC}$. All these marginals are density operators by applying [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]] after grouping factors. Define

$$I(A:B\mid C)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AC})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_C)-S(\rho_{ABC}).$$

These are finite-dimensional definitions only; no non-negativity of conditional entropy or conditional mutual information is part of the notation.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F3] [[lem-it-maximum-coherent-information-attained]]: the finite-dimensional maximum of $S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)$ exists.
citations.quote:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a quantum channel between nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, and fix any finite Stinespring complement $\mathcal N^c:A\to E$. Both functions

$$\rho\longmapsto I_c(\rho,\mathcal N),\qquad \rho\longmapsto S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)$$

attain a maximum on the density operators on $A$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F4] [[lem-it-entanglement-assisted-information-is-additive]]: $F(\mathcal N):=\sup_\rho[S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)]$ is additive for tensor-product channels.
citations.quote:
For a finite-dimensional channel $\mathcal N:A\to B$, define

$$f_{\mathcal N}(\rho):=S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N),\qquad F(\mathcal N):=\sup_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A)}f_{\mathcal N}(\rho).$$

For any two finite-dimensional channels $\mathcal N_i:A_i\to B_i$,

$$F(\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2)=F(\mathcal N_1)+F(\mathcal N_2).$$

citations.exact_fact_text: [F5] [[lem-it-flat-input-entanglement-assisted-achievability]]: Flat-input entanglement-assisted achievability by Weyl coding.
citations.quote: Let $\tau=JJ^*/D$ be the flat state of a nonzero $D$-dimensional input subspace of a finite-dimensional channel $\mathcal N$. With prior shared maximally entangled states on that subspace, every $0\le R<S(\tau)+I_c(\tau,\mathcal N)$ is achievable for classical messages with average error tending to zero. The code consists of finite Weyl operations followed by a collective output/reference POVM; it has rate tending to $R$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F6] [[lem-it-flat-spectral-type-information-approximation]]: Exact flat spectral-type reduction of channel information.
citations.quote: Let $\mathcal N:\mathcal L(A)\to\mathcal L(B)$ be a finite-dimensional channel, let $d=\dim A$, and let $\rho$ be a state on $A$. Fix a finite Stinespring dilation of $\mathcal N$ and its complementary channel. For each integer $n\ge1$ there is an exact decomposition $\rho^{\otimes n}=\sum_t p_t\tau_t$ into mutually orthogonal flat spectral-type states, with at most $(n+1)^d$ positive-weight types and $H(T):=-\sum_{t:p_t>0}p_t\ln p_t\le d\ln(n+1)$. For the fixed complement and its tensor powers, $$\sum_t p_t I_c(\tau_t,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})\ge nI_c(\rho,\mathcal N)-H(T),$$ $$\sum_t p_t[S(\tau_t)+I_c(\tau_t,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})]\ge n[S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)]-2H(T).$$ Thus in each inequality some flat type state attains at least the displayed lower bound.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F7] [[lem-it-finite-extension-from-purification-channel]]: Every finite extension is obtained from a purification by a channel.
citations.quote: Let $\omega_{ZA}$ be any finite-dimensional state with $\operatorname{Tr}_Z\omega_{ZA}=\rho_A$, and let $|\psi\rangle_{RA}$ purify $\rho_A$ with $R$ a copy of $A$. There is a CPTP map $\Lambda:R\to Z$ with $(\Lambda\otimes\operatorname{id}_A)(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)=\omega_{ZA}$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F8] [[thm-it-finite-quantum-mutual-information-data-processing]]: Data processing for finite quantum mutual information.
citations.quote:
Let $A,B,A',B'$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, let $\rho_{AB}$ be a density operator on $A\otimes B$, and let $\Phi:A\to A'$ and $\Psi:B\to B'$ be quantum channels. Then

$$I(A':B')_{(\Phi\otimes\Psi)(\rho)}\le I(A:B)_\rho,$$

where quantum mutual information is $I(X:Y)_\omega=S(\omega_X)+S(\omega_Y)-S(\omega_{XY})$ as in [[def-it-finite-quantum-information-measures]].

citations.exact_fact_text: [F9] [[thm-it-fano-inequality]]: Finite-alphabet Fano inequality.
citations.quote:
Let $X$ take values in an alphabet $\mathcal X$ of size $m\ge2$, let $Y$ be finite, and let $\widehat X$ be an estimator in the same alphabet generated from $Y$, so the joint pmf factors as $p_{XY\widehat X}=p_{XY}p_{\widehat X|Y}$. Put $P_e=\mathbb P[\widehat X\ne X]$ and define

$$h_2(t):=-t\ln t-(1-t)\ln(1-t),\qquad 0\ln0:=0.$$

Then

$$H(X|Y)\le h_2(P_e)+P_e\ln(m-1)\le \ln2+P_e\ln m.$$

For $m=1$, $X$ is constant and $H(X|Y)=0$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F10] [[thm-it-holevo-measurement-bound]]: The finite Holevo measurement bound.
citations.quote:
Let $X$ be a finite nonempty set, let $(p_x)$ be a probability vector, let $\rho_x$ be density operators on a nonzero finite-dimensional space $H_B$, and let $\bar\rho:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x$. For a finite POVM $(E_y)_{y\in Y}$ on $H_B$, define $w(y\mid x):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_xE_y)$, $q_y:=\sum_xp_xw(y\mid x)$, and the classical mutual information

$$I(X:Y):=\sum_{x,y:p_xw(y\mid x)>0}p_xw(y\mid x)\ln\frac{w(y\mid x)}{q_y}.$$

Then

$$I(X:Y)\le\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\})=S(\bar\rho)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x).$$

citations.exact_fact_text: [F11] [[thm-it-finite-entropy-chain-rule]]: for finite classical messages, $I(M;\widehat M)=H(M)-H(M\mid\widehat M)$.
citations.quote:
For finite $X,Y,Z$ with a joint pmf,

$$H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z),$$

and

$$I(X;Y,Z)=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z).$$

In particular, $I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X)$. All terms are finite.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F12] [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]: the natural logarithm product law used by the finite entropy chain rule and type entropy calculation.
citations.quote:
The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,
$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F13] [[thm-logarithm-slower-than-every-positive-power]]: $\ln x/x\to0$ as $x\to\infty$.
citations.quote:
For every $\alpha>0$,
$$\lim_{x\to+\infty}\frac{\log x}{x^\alpha}=0.$$

citations.exact_fact_text: [F14] [[thm-it-finite-strong-subadditivity]]: with a one-dimensional middle register, strong subadditivity gives $S(SB)\le S(S)+S(B)$ and hence $I(S:B)\ge0$.
citations.quote:
Let $H_A,H_B,H_C$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\rho_{ABC}$ be a density operator on their ordered tensor product. Write $\rho_{AB},\rho_{BC},\rho_B$ for its marginals using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]]. Then
$$S(\rho_{AB})+S(\rho_{BC})\ge S(\rho_B)+S(\rho_{ABC}),$$
where $S(\rho)=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho)$ with $0\ln0:=0$ as in [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

citations.exact_fact_text: [F15] [[thm-it-quantum-entropy-identities]]: for the finite cq output ensemble, $I(M:B^nS)$ is its Holevo information; the required logarithm product law is included in [F12].
citations.quote:
For a finite-dimensional bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$,

$$I(A:B)_\rho=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB})=D(\rho_{AB}\|\rho_A\otimes\rho_B).$$

For a finite classical-quantum state $\rho_{XB}=\sum_xp_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x$, its mutual information equals its Holevo information:

$$I(X:B)_\rho=S\!\left(\sum_xp_x\rho_x\right)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x)=\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}).$$

derivations.claim: For any purification $\psi_{RA}$, its reference marginal is $\rho_R$ with the same positive eigenvalues as $\rho_A$, so $S(R)=S(\rho)$ by [F1]. Substituting [F1] into [F2] gives $I(R;B)=S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)$. Thus the two maximized information expressions in the Statement agree, and [F3] supplies their maximizers.

By [F4], the optimized one-use information is additive across every finite tensor power; hence its regularized information value is the same one-use maximum. This proves additivity for the information expression itself.

For any input state $\rho$ and positive integer $m$, exact spectral type reduction gives a flat state $\tau_t$ on an $m$-use input subspace such that $$f_{\mathcal N^{\otimes m}}(\tau_t)\ge m f_{\mathcal N}(\rho)-2d\ln(m+1),\qquad d=\dim A.$$ Apply the flat-state construction to that fixed block channel. For fixed $m$, both its Weyl alphabet and its receiver output dimension are finite, so the HSW theorem applies before any limit in $m$ is taken. The shared resource is the flat type-subspace maximally entangled state for each outer block. Padding fewer than $m$ unused original-channel inputs with a fixed state gives codes for all sufficiently large lengths and no asymptotic rate loss. Therefore $$C_E(\mathcal N)\ge f_{\mathcal N}(\rho)-\frac{2d\ln(m+1)}m.$$ Since $\ln(m+1)/m\to0$ by [F13], letting $m\to\infty$ and maximizing over $\rho$ proves the general direct bound with precisely the stated unlimited finite-shared-entanglement model. No unrestricted quantum-input HSW single-letter theorem and no inference from Schumacher compression alone is used.

Consider any length-$n$ stated EA code with uniform message register $M$, receiver's prior share $S$, channel input $A^n$, and receiver output $B^nS$. Before transmission its joint state is $$\omega_{MA^nS}=\frac1K\sum_m|m\rangle\langle m|\otimes(\mathcal E_m\otimes\operatorname{id}_S)(\sigma).$$ The marginal $MS$ is the product of the uniform message and the original share: each encoder is trace-preserving and hence cannot change $S$. In particular $I(M:S)=0$. Let $\bar\rho_{A^n}$ be its average input. By the extension lemma, the $MSA^n$ state is obtained by a channel on the reference of a purification of $\bar\rho_{A^n}$. After transmission, quantum-mutual-information data processing gives $$I(MS:B^n)\le I(R:B^n)_{(\operatorname{id}\otimes\mathcal N^{\otimes n})(\psi_{\bar\rho})}.$$ Expanding the entropy definitions gives the exact identity $$I(M:B^nS)=I(MS:B^n)-I(S:B^n)+I(M:S).$$ The last term is zero, and [F14] gives $I(S:B^n)\ge0$. Therefore $$I(M:B^nS)\le I(R:B^n)\le F(\mathcal N^{\otimes n})=nF(\mathcal N).$$ The equality uses the stated optimized-information additivity lemma, whose proof follows local-channel mutual-information data processing and product-state entropy additivity. Write $h(u)=-u\ln u-(1-u)\ln(1-u)$ with continuous endpoint values. By [F11], $I(M;\widehat M)=H(M)-H(M\mid\widehat M)$; [F15] identifies $I(M:B^nS)$ with the Holevo quantity of the cq output state, and the Holevo measurement bound [F10] gives $I(M;\widehat M)\le I(M:B^nS)$. Fano then gives $$(1-e_n)\ln K_n\le nF(\mathcal N)+h(e_n).$$ Singleton message sets are trivial. Divide by $n$ and let average error tend to zero to bound every achievable rate by $F(\mathcal N)$, without restricting the shared state, its dimension, or the message-dependent CPTP encoders. Together with the general direct bound, purification identity and attained maximum, this proves the entire retained operational formula. Finally applying the identity $C_E=F$ to both channels and their product, and using the stated proved additivity of $F$, proves the capacity additivity assertion as well.

For finite $X,Y,Z$ with a joint pmf,

$$H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z),$$

and

citations.exact_fact_text: [F1] [[def-it-finite-conditional-entropy]]: $H(U|V)=\sum_{v:p_V(v)>0}p_V(v)H(p_{U|v})$, with zero-mass conditioning values omitted.
citations.quote:
Let $p_{XY}$ be a joint probability vector on finite alphabets $\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y$. It is the weight function of the canonical finite probability space from [[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]; its coordinate maps are finite random elements in the sense of [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]. Write $p_Y(y)=\sum_xp_{XY}(x,y)$. For each $y$ with $p_Y(y)>0$, set $p_{X|y}(x)=p_{XY}(x,y)/p_Y(y)$; this is a probability vector by [[lem-it-finite-marginals-and-conditionals-are-pmfs]]. Define the conditional entropy in nats by

$$H(X|Y):=\sum_{y:p_Y(y)>0}p_Y(y)H(p_{X|y}),$$

where $H(p)=-\sum_xp(x)\ln p(x)$ is the finite entropy of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]]. Terms for zero-mass $y$ are omitted. The base-$b$ version replaces $\ln$ by $\log_b$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F2] [[def-it-finite-mutual-information]]: $I(U;V)=\sum_{p_{UV}(u,v)>0}p_{UV}(u,v)\ln[p_{UV}(u,v)/(p_U(u)p_V(v))]$.
citations.quote:
Let $p_{XY}$ be a joint probability vector on finite alphabets $\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y$, with marginals $p_X(x):=\sum_y p_{XY}(x,y)$ and $p_Y(y):=\sum_xp_{XY}(x,y)$. The marginals are probability vectors by [[lem-it-finite-marginals-and-conditionals-are-pmfs]]. The joint vector is the outcome-weight function of the canonical finite probability space from [[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]; its coordinate maps are finite random elements in the sense of [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]. Define mutual information in nats by

$$I(X;Y):=D(p_{XY}\|p_X\otimes p_Y)=\sum_{(x,y):p_{XY}(x,y)>0}p_{XY}(x,y)\ln\frac{p_{XY}(x,y)}{p_X(x)p_Y(y)},$$

where $D$ is the finite KL convention of [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]] and $(p_X\otimes p_Y)(x,y):=p_X(x)p_Y(y)$. Every ratio in the displayed sum is positive and finite: if $p_{XY}(x,y)>0$, then each marginal sum is at least that positive entry. The sum is over finite support, so $I(X;Y)$ is finite. The base-$b$ version replaces $\ln$ by $\log_b$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F3] [[thm-it-finite-conditional-mutual-information-identities-and-equality]]: $I(X;Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|Z)-H(X,Y|Z)$.
citations.quote:
For finite $X,Y,Z$,

$$I(X;Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|Z)-H(X,Y|Z)\ge0.$$

Equality holds if and only if, for every $z$ with $p_Z(z)>0$, the conditional joint pmf factors as $p_{XY|z}=p_{X|z}p_{Y|z}$; this is conditional independence given $Z$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F4] [[lem-it-finite-marginals-and-conditionals-are-pmfs]]: conditional pmfs are formed by division by positive marginal mass and are probability vectors.
citations.quote: Let $\mathcal U,\mathcal V$ be finite nonempty alphabets and let $p_{UV}(u,v)\ge0$ satisfy $\sum_{u,v}p_{UV}(u,v)=1$. Define $p_U(u)=\sum_vp_{UV}(u,v)$ and $p_V(v)=\sum_up_{UV}(u,v)$. Then both marginals are probability vectors. For each $v$ with $p_V(v)>0$, the conditional vector $p_{U|v}(u):=p_{UV}(u,v)/p_V(v)$ is a probability vector; likewise for conditioning on positive-mass $u$. Consequently, if $p_{UVW}$ is a finite joint pmf, then for every $w$ with $p_W(w)>0$, $p_{UV|w}$ and its two marginals are probability vectors.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F5] [[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]]: $H(p)=-\sum_{p_i>0}p_i\ln p_i$, with $0\ln0=0$.
citations.quote:
For a finite nonempty set identified with $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$, a **probability vector** is $p=(p_i)_{i=1}^k$ with $p_i\ge0$ and $\sum_i p_i=1$; it is the outcome-weight vector of a finite probability space ([[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]). Its Shannon entropy in natural units is
$$H(p):=-\sum_{i=1}^k p_i\ln p_i,$$
with $0\ln0:=0$. For probability vectors $p,q$ on the same set $[k]$, the relative entropy is
$$D(p\|q):=\sum_{i:p_i>0}p_i\ln(p_i/q_i),$$
with value $+\infty$ if $p_i>0=q_i$ for some $i$. A matrix $A\in[0,1]^{N\times m}$ is **row-stochastic** when each row sums to one. For a probability row vector $p$ on $[m]$ and a row vector $X\in[0,1]^m$, the dot product $pX^{\mathsf T}=\sum_{i=1}^m p_iX_i$ is the acceptance probability under distribution $p$.

These definitions use finite sets only; entropy is between $0$ and $\ln k$, as proved where needed below.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F6] [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]: for positive $x,y$, $\ln(xy)=\ln x+\ln y$ and $\ln(x/y)=\ln x-\ln y$.
citations.quote:
The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,
$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

derivations.claim: Fix $z$ with $p_Z(z)>0$ and write $q_{xy}=p_{XY|z}(x,y)$, $q_x=\sum_yq_{xy}$; for $q_x>0$ define $q_{y|x}=q_{xy}/q_x$. By [F4], these are pmfs and $q_{xy}=q_xq_{y|x}$ on positive support. On the positive support both factors are positive, so the product law [F6] gives $-\sum_{q_{xy}>0}q_{xy}\ln q_{xy}=-\sum_{q_x>0,y}q_xq_{y|x}(\ln q_x+\ln q_{y|x})$. Since $\sum_yq_{y|x}=1$, the first sum is $-\sum_{q_x>0}q_x\ln q_x$ and the second is $\sum_{q_x>0}q_x(-\sum_{q_{y|x}>0}q_{y|x}\ln q_{y|x})$, exactly $H(q_X)+\sum_xq_xH(q_{Y|x})$ by [F5]. Weighting this equality by $p_Z(z)$ and summing over positive-mass $z$ using [F1] proves $H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z)$. Zero atoms contribute zero by convention.

Every positive joint atom has positive marginals by [F4]; applying the quotient and product laws [F6] to [F2] gives $I(U;V)=\sum_{p_{uv}>0}p_{uv}(\ln p_{uv}-\ln p_U(u)-\ln p_V(v))$. Grouping the finite sums by $u,v$, using [F4] to know the marginals, and applying [F5] yields $I(U;V)=H(U)+H(V)-H(U,V)$. Also, [F1] and $p_{U|v}=p_{UV}/p_V$ on positive support give $H(U|V)=-\sum_{p_{uv}>0}p_{uv}\ln(p_{uv}/p_V(v))=H(U,V)-H(V)$. Thus $I(U;V)=H(U)-H(U|V)$, and exchanging $U,V$ gives the other form. All sums are finite.

Apply step 1.1 and [F3] to get $I(X;Y|Z)=H(Y|Z)-H(Y|X,Z)$. By step 1.2, $H(Y,Z)=H(Z)+H(Y|Z)$ and $H(X,Y,Z)=H(Z)+H(X,Y|Z)=H(X,Z)+H(Y|X,Z)$. Therefore $I(X;Y,Z)=H(X)+H(Y,Z)-H(X,Y,Z)=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z)$. Every entropy is a finite sum, so no extended-real subtraction occurs.

Let $A,B,A',B'$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, let $\rho_{AB}$ be a density operator on $A\otimes B$, and let $\Phi:A\to A'$ and $\Psi:B\to B'$ be quantum channels. Then

$$I(A':B')_{(\Phi\otimes\Psi)(\rho)}\le I(A:B)_\rho,$$

where quantum mutual information is $I(X:Y)_\omega=S(\omega_X)+S(\omega_Y)-S(\omega_{XY})$ as in [[def-it-finite-quantum-information-measures]].

citations.exact_fact_text: [F1] [[def-it-finite-quantum-information-measures]]: $I(X:Y)=S(X)+S(Y)-S(XY)$ for finite bipartite states.
citations.quote:
For a finite bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B$, write $\rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho_{AB}$ and $\rho_B=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$, using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]] and [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]. They are states by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. Define

$$S(A)_\rho:=S(\rho_A),\qquad S(A\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})-S(\rho_B),\qquad I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a finite tripartite state $\rho_{ABC}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, set $\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_C}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying the factors as $(H_A\otimes H_B)\otimes H_C$, and $\rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_A}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying them as $H_A\otimes(H_B\otimes H_C)$. Let $P:H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C\to H_A\otimes H_C\otimes H_B$ be the wire permutation taking factor order $A,B,C$ to $A,C,B$ ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]) whose unique adjoint $P^*$ exists by [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]], and set $\rho_{AC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}(P\rho_{ABC}P^*)$, tracing out the last factor. Because $P$ is unitary, $P\rho_{ABC}P^*$ is a state: unitary conjugation preserves non-negativity by the adjoint identity ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]) and preserves trace by cyclicity ([[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]). Finally set $\rho_C:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\rho_{BC}$. All these marginals are density operators by applying [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]] after grouping factors. Define

$$I(A:B\mid C)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AC})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_C)-S(\rho_{ABC}).$$

These are finite-dimensional definitions only; no non-negativity of conditional entropy or conditional mutual information is part of the notation.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F2] [[thm-it-finite-strong-subadditivity]]: for every finite tripartite state $\omega_{XYZ}$, $S(XY)+S(YZ)\ge S(Y)+S(XYZ)$.
citations.quote:
Let $H_A,H_B,H_C$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\rho_{ABC}$ be a density operator on their ordered tensor product. Write $\rho_{AB},\rho_{BC},\rho_B$ for its marginals using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]]. Then
$$S(\rho_{AB})+S(\rho_{BC})\ge S(\rho_B)+S(\rho_{ABC}),$$
where $S(\rho)=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho)$ with $0\ln0:=0$ as in [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

citations.exact_fact_text: [F3] [[thm-qc-finite-stinespring-dilation]]: each finite-dimensional channel has an isometric dilation $V$ with output obtained by tracing its finite environment.
citations.quote:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be a quantum channel. It has a finite
Kraus representation, and for any chosen such representation with $N$
operators $K_a:H\to K$ there are an $N$-dimensional environment $E$ and a
linear isometry $V:H\to K\otimes E$ such that
$$\Phi(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^\dagger)\quad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H).$$

citations.exact_fact_text: [F4] [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]: positive operators have finite orthonormal spectral decompositions.
citations.quote:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F5] [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]: partial traces of finite-dimensional density operators are density operators.
citations.quote: For nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_A,H_B$ and a density operator $\rho_{AB}$ on $H_A\otimes H_B$, both marginals $\rho_A:=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho_{AB}$ and $\rho_B:=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$ are density operators.

citations.exact_fact_text: [F6] [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]] and [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]: factors may be reordered by a unitary wire permutation, preserving the state and its entropy.
citations.quote:
An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

citations.exact_fact_text: [F6] [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]] and [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]: factors may be reordered by a unitary wire permutation, preserving the state and its entropy.
citations.quote:
Let $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$ be a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces, with the product bases of
[[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For a permutation $\sigma$ of the
factor positions, the map $P_\sigma$ that reorders the factors is a bijective
linear isometry from $H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$ to
$H_{\sigma(0)}\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{\sigma(n-1)}$. When source and target
are identified as the same register, $P_\sigma$ is a unitary operator in the
sense of [[def-linear-isometry-and-orthogonal-or-unitary-operator]].

$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

derivations.claim: First apply $\Phi$ to $A$. Choose a Stinespring isometry $V:A\to A'\otimes E$ from [F3], and form $\widetilde\rho_{A'EB}:=(V\otimes I_B)\rho_{AB}(V^*\otimes I_B)$. This is a state: a spectral decomposition of $\rho_{AB}$ in [F4] shows that its nonzero eigenvalues remain the same under the isometric embedding. Its $A'E$ marginal is $V\rho_A V^*$ and has the same positive eigenvalues as $\rho_A$, while its $A'EB$ joint state has the same positive eigenvalues as $\rho_{AB}$. Thus [F1] gives $I(A'E:B)_{\widetilde\rho}=I(A:B)_\rho$.

Reorder $A'EB$ to $EA'B$ by the unitary permutation in [F6]. Apply [F2] to the ordered tripartite state $\widetilde\rho_{EA'B}$, with $A'=Y$, to obtain $S(EA')+S(A'B)\ge S(A')+S(EA'B)$. Rearranging by [F1] gives $I(EA':B)\ge I(A':B)$. The entropy identities and their logarithm product law are supplied by [F7]. The $A'B$ marginal is $(\Phi\otimes\operatorname{id}_B)(\rho)$ by [F3] and the partial-trace convention; hence applying $\Phi$ cannot increase mutual information.

Repeat step 1.1–2.1 with $\Psi$ acting on the second register, now taking the first register to be $A'$. This gives $I(A':B')_{(\Phi\otimes\Psi)(\rho)}\le I(A':B)_{(\Phi\otimes\operatorname{id}_B)(\rho)}$. Combine this with step 2.1 to obtain the claimed inequality. The entropy-law prerequisite remains [F7].
